title: Formal Verification of Domain-Specific Languages
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to formal verification by introducing a Domain-Specific Language (DSL) tailored for specific domains such as security and embedded systems. The core claim is that designing a specialized DSL significantly improves verification efficiency and reliability compared to general-purpose formal verification languages. The proposed mechanism leverages domain knowledge to create a language with precise modeling capabilities and integrated automated verification tools, minimizing the need for manual intervention. The current landscape of formal verification languages suffers from a lack of domain-specific optimization, leading to inefficiencies and increased complexity. This DSL addresses these limitations by providing a streamlined and targeted approach to verification. The paper outlines the key design principles, formal semantics, and potential applications of this DSL. ---

title: Quantum Hidden Matrix Geometry Optimization and Topology
abstract: Quantum Hidden Matrix Geometry Optimization and Topology addresses the challenge of optimizing quantum computation by employing a novel adaptive geometric optimization algorithm. This algorithm leverages the dynamic evolution of quantum states to iteratively refine the quantum state, ultimately aiming to enhance the efficiency and stability of quantum calculations. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting the quantum potential field to guide the system towards a more optimal configuration. This approach distinguishes itself from traditional methods by offering a flexible and adaptive optimization strategy. The resulting optimization process contributes to improved computational performance and robustness. This paper presents a comprehensive investigation of the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance evaluation, highlighting its potential impact on quantum computing.

title: Annotated Marathi Word Sense Disambiguation Dataset
abstract: This dataset is a large-scale sense-annotated resource for Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD) in Marathi, a morphologically rich and relatively low-resource Indic language. It was developed to address the limited availability of reusable, sense-annotated Marathi corpora for supervised WSD research. The final dataset contains 50,242 binary sentence–gloss pair records, covering 16 ambiguous Marathi words and 50 distinct senses across different grammatical categories, including nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, and postpositions. The target words and their candidate senses were derived from the Marathi WordNet. Naturally occurring Marathi sentences were collected from established Marathi news portals and blogs, including Loksatta, Esakal, Lokmat, ABP Live Marathi, BBC Marathi, TV9 Marathi, News18 Marathi, Maharashtra Times, Mitraho, Marathi Spandan, and Maayboli. The collected text was cleaned, sentence-segmented, filtered based on sentence length, and duplicate sentences were removed to obtain a suitable corpus for WSD. Since Marathi exhibits substantial inflectional variation, the Stanford Stanza Marathi lemmatizer was used to identify target words in their different morphological forms. A prefix-based matching strategy was additionally applied when lemmatization failed for particular cases. For each word-sense pair, seed sentences were generated using the corresponding Marathi WordNet gloss and manually reviewed for clarity, grammatical correctness, and sense consistency. These verified examples were subsequently used as reference sentences for constructing sense representations. Candidate sentences were assigned to senses using MuRIL token-level embeddings and cosine similarity. A similarity threshold of 0.65 was used for the primary assignment, while a relaxed threshold of 0.60 was used for controlled padding of underrepresented senses. The dataset follows a binary sentence–gloss pair formulation. For every sentence containing an ambiguous target word, the sentence is paired with each candidate sense gloss. The correct sentence–sense pairing receives label 1, whereas incorrect pairings receive label 0. This structure makes the dataset suitable for cross-encoder WSD models and also allows conversion into a conventional multi-class classification format. Each record contains seven fields: sentence, target_word, lemma, pos, sense_id, gloss, and label. The dataset can be used for Marathi WSD benchmarking, supervised learning, transformer-based cross-encoder research, lexical-semantic analysis, contextual representation learning, and NLP research for low-resource Indic languages.

title: Navigating to Interact: A Dual‐Graph Framework Orchestrating Semantic Exploration and Local Positioning for Household Assisting Robots
abstract: Performing tasks for household assisting robots in complex, multi‐room environments requires embodied agents to accomplish long‐horizon cross‐room navigation and precise object interaction. However, existing approaches typically focus either on visual navigation without physical interaction or on manipulation tasks restricted to single‐room environments. To address these challenges, we propose a hierarchical framework that combines global semantic exploration with local interaction‐aware positioning. At the global level, a Dual‐Graph Navigation policy maintains a Dynamic Scene Topology Graph for online spatial memory and leverages a Prior Knowledge Graph to guide target‐oriented search through semantic object‐object correlations. At the local level, an Interaction‐Oriented Positioning module identifies interaction‐feasible docking poses on local occupancy maps for reliable manipulation. Extensive experiments on the large‐scale ProcTHOR‐10 k benchmark demonstrate that our framework achieves robust performance in navigation efficiency and task success rate, verifying its effectiveness in successfully accomplishing complex household tasks in diverse, procedurally generated environments. © 2026 Institute of Electrical Engineers of Japan and Wiley Periodicals LLC.

title: LATS: Levy Adaptive Tree Sampling for Feedback-Driven Diverse Target Discovery
abstract: While diffusion models excel at capturing complex data distributions, scientific discovery often requires steering generation toward specific, uncharacterized regions that maximize a target objective. These high-utility modes frequently reside in low-likelihood tail regions and are only revealed sequentially through interactive feedback. Existing diffusion samplers fail in this regime: they inherit the pre-trained model's bias toward high-density regions, leaving rare yet promising phenomena underexplored. Conversely, exploration-heavy samplers ensure broad coverage but fail to efficiently exploit high-utility modes when constrained by a strict sampling budget. To resolve this dilemma, we introduce Levy Adaptive Tree Search (LATS), a principled sampling framework for online feedback-driven search. LATS leverages heavy-tailed exploration coupled with tree-based value backpropagation to progressively uncover preferred modes. By maintaining broad distributional coverage, LATS successfully discovers low-likelihood, high-utility regions while preserving sample fidelity and structural diversity. Experiments across diverse benchmarks, including materials science, demonstrate that LATS significantly outperforms baselines in target discovery efficiency.

title: One MLLM, One Call: Efficient Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation via Spatial-Aware Waypoints
abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE) requires an embodied agent to navigate unseen environments by following natural language instructions. Current zero-shot VLN-CE methods either rely on pre-trained waypoint predictors or require multiple queries to large models per step. To address prohibitive inference latency and computational overhead, we propose O2C-Nav, an efficient zero-shot navigation framework that calls only a single large model once per decision step. Our approach introduces a training-free structured waypoint generator and a novel abstract representation that projects sparse, history-aware candidate waypoints directly onto RGB images as visual markers. The MLLM selects a waypoint or generates a fallback target bounding box at each step, while a low-level Fast Marching Method (FMM) planner converts the selected target into an executable collision-free path. This paradigm provides the model with concrete spatial perception and explicit memory while significantly reducing the visual processing load. Extensive evaluations on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks demonstrate that O2C-Nav outperforms current state-of-the-art zero-shot methods, highlighting its great potential for real-time robotic deployment. Code is available at https://github.com/kkpsq/O2C-Nav-Code.

title: 基于自适应的分布式优化算法的量子模拟
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum simulation technique leveraging a dynamically adaptive distributed optimization algorithm. Traditional quantum simulation methods are often static, limiting efficiency and precision. Our approach dynamically adjusts quantum simulation parameters to optimize performance, resulting in significant improvements in simulation speed and accuracy. We present a framework designed to achieve this dynamic adjustment, offering a promising pathway for efficient and precise quantum system analysis. The core mechanism involves a self-optimizing quantum simulator, enhancing simulation capabilities. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through simulations of complex quantum systems.

title: Reproduction package for "What Does a Factual-Error Detector Really Measure? Question Difficulty and Model Uncertainty Before the Answer Begins"
abstract: Original inputs, analysis scripts, reference results and frozen preregistrations for the article "What Does a Factual-Error Detector Really Measure? Question Difficulty and Model Uncertainty Before the Answer Begins" (submitted to Information Sciences). The package covers a main panel of 17 open-weight instruction-tuned models (2,380 short factual questions; 18,850 model–question pairs; stored labels and activation-derived features around the answer onset), three replication corpora (Natural Questions, BioASQ, TriviaQA; 18 models), a clean-design replication (9 models × 3,993 shared questions), the stored greedy and sampled answers, the question packs with reference aliases, the responses with the answer tokens marked in the extraction pipeline, the extraction scripts used on GPU, and a fail-fast runner (run_all.sh) that recomputes the 11 result files behind the article's claims and compares every value with the reference results (86,212 values, tolerance 1e-6; last clean run 2026-09-05). Also included: the label audit against two independent human annotators, the frozen preregistrations with their commit stamps, and auxiliary result files cited in the supplement. See README_EN.md (quick start) and README_REPRODUCTION.md (full change log, in Polish). Raw activation tensors (8.1 TB) are not included; they can be regenerated with the extraction scripts and the public model weights referenced in the data files.

title: Core Claim: A novel adaptive quantum circuit optimization algorithm that dynamically adjusts circuit performance based on quantum circuit dynamics, achieving more efficient quantum computation.
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for scientific discovery and technological advancement, but the design and optimization of quantum circuits remain a significant challenge. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static circuit configurations, limiting the potential for enhanced performance. This paper introduces a novel adaptive quantum circuit optimization algorithm, termed "Dynamic Quantum Tuning" (DQT), that leverages the dynamic evolution of quantum circuits to guide circuit optimization. DQT dynamically adjusts circuit parameters based on real-time feedback, resulting in significantly improved circuit performance and increased computational efficiency. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that monitors the circuit's output, adjusts parameters, and repeats this process, continuously refining the circuit's optimal configuration. This approach overcomes the limitations of static optimization, offering a paradigm shift towards adaptive and efficient quantum algorithm design. We present experimental results demonstrating the superior performance of DQT across a range of quantum circuit tasks, highlighting its potential to accelerate quantum computation.

title: Adaptive Self-Adaptation Learning
abstract: This paper investigates a novel adaptive self-adaptation learning algorithm, termed Adaptive Self-Adaptation Learning (ASAL), designed to enhance model generalization and adaptability. Traditional machine learning methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting their ability to effectively learn complex data distributions. ASAL leverages graph-based representations to model data relationships, dynamically adjusting model parameters based on observed data patterns. The core mechanism centers around a graph structure that allows for continuous parameter refinement, leading to improved predictive performance. This research presents a framework for dynamically adjusting model parameters through a graph-based representation, offering a significant advancement over existing techniques.

title: System Modeling with Adaptive Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive neural networks to system modeling, focusing on the development of a method that learns adaptive features and predicts system behavior. Traditional system modeling often relies on extensive training data, while our approach leverages adaptive learning to minimize data requirements. We present a novel framework incorporating a self-learning neural network to automatically extract and refine features crucial for accurate prediction. The core mechanism centers around training a neural network to identify and represent key characteristics of a system, enabling predictive capabilities that surpass traditional methods. The resulting model demonstrates improved accuracy and robustness in a variety of system modeling tasks.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computation Device
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same fate, presents a unique opportunity for computation. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to design a novel computational device, tentatively termed the "Quantum Entanglement Computation Device" (QECD). We outline the core claim, outlining a design approach focusing on harnessing entanglement for enhanced parallel processing and information transfer within the device's architecture, aiming to surpass the limitations of classical computing. The paper will detail the core mechanism, illustrating how entanglement is utilized to enable significantly increased computational speed and efficiency.

title: Quantum Entangled Matrix Topology Analysis and Computation
abstract: This paper investigates the topological properties of quantum entangled matrices, exploring their potential for enhanced security and efficiency in quantum computation. We introduce the concept of a "拓扑隐形矩阵" – a matrix whose structure is fundamentally altered through a complex topological process – and demonstrate its application in mitigating computational challenges. The core mechanism centers on leveraging these topological properties to reduce computational complexity while simultaneously bolstering security through a novel approach to error correction. This research seeks to provide a fundamentally new framework for safeguarding quantum information, moving beyond traditional cryptographic methods.

title: Title: Adaptive Probability Field Model Dynamic Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive probability field model dynamic optimization algorithm designed to efficiently optimize and predict system behavior in dynamic environments. Traditional optimization algorithms typically rely on static parameter adjustments, offering limited adaptability to real-world variations. Our proposed approach utilizes a dynamic probabilistic model, allowing the model to dynamically adjust its parameters based on the system's operating conditions. This adaptive nature enhances the algorithm's robustness and facilitates faster convergence and improved predictive accuracy. The core mechanism centers around a novel probability field self-adaptation process, which continuously refines the model's representation of the system's dynamics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through extensive simulations and comparisons with established optimization techniques.

title: Self-Correcting Digital Circuits via Quantum Annealing
abstract: Digital circuits, the backbone of modern computation, are increasingly vulnerable to errors arising from environmental noise, including electromagnetic interference, thermal fluctuations, and process variations. These errors can propagate through circuits, leading to unreliable operation and potentially catastrophic failures, particularly in critical applications like aerospace, defense, and high-performance computing. This paper proposes a novel approach to mitigating these errors by leveraging the principles of Quantum Annealing (QA) to create self-correcting digital circuits. The core concept involves dynamically optimizing the circuit's design and operational parameters in real-time, responding to detected noise and implementing corrective actions. We formulate the circuit self-correction problem as an optimization problem amenable to QA. The objective function incorporates error detection metrics and the desired circuit performance. The QA algorithm iteratively explores the design space, identifying configurations that minimize the impact of noise and achieve the target functionality. Mathematical formulations detail the error modeling, the optimization problem, and the QA algorithm's core steps. The proposed method offers a fundamentally new approach to circuit design and operation, potentially leading to significantly more robust and reliable digital systems.

title: ##基于神经符号计算的知识推理引擎 (NSIRE)
abstract: This paper introduces the Neuro-Symbolic Inference Reasoning Engine (NSIRE), a novel system designed to automate knowledge reasoning by integrating the strengths of neural networks and symbolic logic. The core claim driving NSIRE is that a seamless combination of these approaches can significantly improve the efficiency and robustness of knowledge inference tasks. The system operates by representing knowledge as both symbolic structures and neural networks, leveraging neural networks for inference and employing symbolic logic for verification and constraint satisfaction. NSIRE distinguishes itself from traditional rule-based reasoning systems by offering an automated approach to knowledge inference, eliminating the need for manually crafted rules and reducing the risk of human error. This paper details the architecture of NSIRE, its key components, and outlines a potential framework for its application in various domains. The system aims to provide a flexible and adaptable solution for intelligent reasoning, bridging the gap between symbolic and sub-symbolic approaches.

title: Dynamic Programming with Quantum State Tomography for Stochastic Control
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to stochastic control problems by integrating quantum state tomography with dynamic programming. Traditional dynamic programming relies on accurate state representations, which can be challenging to obtain for complex, stochastic systems. Quantum state tomography offers a potentially superior method for characterizing system states, providing a more complete and precise description than classical methods. This work proposes a framework where quantum state tomography is performed at each time step within a dynamic programming algorithm. The resulting quantum state information is then used to construct and execute the dynamic programming process, leading to the discovery of potentially more efficient and robust control policies. The core claim is that this combined approach allows for more accurate state representation and, consequently, improved control. The paper outlines the key elements of this framework and highlights the potential benefits of this synergistic combination of quantum information theory and control theory. The theoretical framework presented demonstrates a pathway towards achieving superior stochastic control solutions compared to traditional approaches.

title: Algorithmic Transparency via Formal Verification of Neural Network Explainability Methods
abstract: The increasing deployment of neural networks in critical applications necessitates a deeper understanding of their decision-making processes – a field commonly addressed through explainability methods. However, current explainability techniques often rely on approximations and heuristics, lacking rigorous guarantees about their accuracy and reliability. This work introduces a novel approach to validate neural network explainability methods by leveraging formal verification techniques, specifically model checking. Our core claim is that many existing explainability methods fail to provide sufficient assurance regarding their correctness. We propose a mechanism for rigorously proving the accuracy of these algorithms by formally verifying their ability to faithfully represent the underlying decision-making process of the neural network. This framework provides a foundation for building more trustworthy and reliable AI systems.

title: Quantum-Inspired Simulation of Complex Fluid Dynamics
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to simulating complex fluid dynamics, specifically turbulent flows, utilizing quantum-inspired algorithms. Traditional numerical methods, such as Navier-Stokes solvers, often struggle with the computational demands of accurately representing turbulence, leading to significant processing times and limitations in practical applications. We introduce a simulation strategy based on quantum amplitude estimation (QAE), a technique inspired by quantum computing principles, to accelerate the solution process. The core idea is to approximate the probability amplitude associated with different fluid states, thereby reducing the number of iterations required to reach a stable solution. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and a simplified numerical framework, that QAE offers a promising path toward more efficient and accurate simulations of turbulent flows, potentially bridging the gap between classical computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and the computational benefits anticipated from full-scale quantum simulation. This work lays the groundwork for future research exploring the full potential of quantum-inspired algorithms in tackling complex fluid dynamics problems.

title: Graph-Based Bayesian Networks for Causal Discovery
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to causal discovery leveraging graph-based Bayesian networks. Traditional causal discovery algorithms often encounter difficulties when dealing with intricate graph structures, leading to inaccurate or incomplete causal models. Our method addresses this limitation by integrating Bayesian network principles with graph-based reasoning, allowing for iterative refinement of the graph structure based on observed statistical dependencies while enforcing causal consistency constraints. The core of our approach lies in utilizing algorithms like PC algorithm and its variants to identify conditional dependencies between variables. We introduce a framework that dynamically updates the graph structure, prioritizing connections that align with both statistical dependence and causal assumptions. The resulting Bayesian network provides a more robust and scalable solution for causal inference, particularly in scenarios with high-dimensional data and complex relationships. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through a theoretical analysis and outlined within the framework of conditional independence tests. Future research directions include exploring hybrid approaches combining this method with reinforcement learning and incorporating domain-specific knowledge to further enhance the accuracy of causal models.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence through Causal Modeling
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) that leverages causal modeling to enhance the transparency and trustworthiness of AI systems. Current XAI techniques often prioritize interpretability without considering the underlying causal relationships governing the data. We introduce a framework that utilizes causal graphs to represent domain knowledge and incorporates machine learning algorithms for inference, leading to more robust and explainable decision-making. The core claim is to design an AI model capable of reasoning and decision-making based on causal relationships, thereby improving transparency and trust. The mechanism involves constructing causal models using causal graphs and integrating machine learning algorithms for inference. This approach addresses a critical gap in existing XAI methods by explicitly incorporating causal reasoning, offering a pathway towards AI systems that not only explain their decisions but also understand the true causal drivers behind them. This work lays the foundation for building more reliable and justifiable AI systems across various domains.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Entropy Encoding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel entropy encoding scheme, termed Dynamic Adaptive Entropy Encoding, designed to overcome the limitations of traditional static encoding methods. The core concept revolves around utilizing real-time system state feedback to dynamically adjust encoding parameters, optimizing for the evolving statistical characteristics of the data stream. We introduce the concept of "state entropy," leveraging machine learning models to predict the data stream's statistical distribution and subsequently tailoring Huffman tree parameters or arithmetic coding settings based on this predicted state entropy. This adaptive approach significantly improves encoding efficiency, particularly in scenarios with non-stationary data streams. The proposed method offers a fundamentally different perspective compared to existing approaches, addressing the inherent inefficiency of fixed-parameter encoding schemes. The primary contribution lies in the dynamic adaptation mechanism driven by real-time statistical analysis and the introduction of a quantifiable metric – state entropy – for guiding the encoding process. Experimental results (simulated) demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme in various data stream scenarios, showcasing a substantial improvement in compression ratios compared to conventional static encoding techniques.

title: Analyse linguistique des commentaires des touristes sur la plateforme numérique Booking : étude des facteurs de satisfaction au Sénégal
abstract: Cette recherche examine, à partir d'une analyse linguistique outillée, les facteurs de satisfaction et d'insatisfaction exprimés par les touristes ayant séjourné dans des établissements d'hébergement sénégalais référencés sur Booking.com. À partir d'un plan d'échantillonnage stratifié par pôle touristique (Dakar, Thiès-Diourbel, Casamance, Sine Saloum, Nord et Sénégal oriental), un corpus de 372 commentaires exploitables a été constitué et soumis à une chaîne de traitement combinant statistique textuelle, traitement automatique du langage naturel (tokenisation, lemmatisation, suppression des mots vides), analyse lexicométrique (fréquences, TF-IDF, n-grammes, champs lexicaux, réseau de cooccurrences), modélisation thématique (Latent Dirichlet Allocation) et analyse des sentiments globale et par aspects (Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis, ABSA), cette dernière reposant sur un dictionnaire lexical spécialisé dans le domaine hôtelier en raison de l'indisponibilité, dans l'environnement de traitement, des modèles neuronaux pré-entraînés de type CamemBERT ou XLM-RoBERTa. Les résultats indiquent une tonalité globalement positive du corpus (73,4 % des commentaires), portée principalement par la qualité de l'accueil et du personnel, la propreté et le calme des lieux, tandis que le confort des chambres, le rapport qualité-prix et, dans une moindre mesure, la connexion internet concentrent les motifs d'insatisfaction.

title: Title: Dynamically Adaptive Constraint Propagation in Quantum Networks
abstract: Quantum networks represent a revolutionary paradigm for quantum computing and communication, offering unprecedented capabilities for complex calculations. However, the inherent fragility of quantum states necessitates sophisticated techniques for managing entanglement and quantum information. This paper explores the use of dynamically adaptive constraint propagation within quantum networks to enhance solution finding for complex problems. We propose a novel algorithm that monitors the quantum state of nodes and adapts constraint propagation accordingly, improving the network's ability to solve problems with intricate relationships. The core mechanism involves a quantum algorithm that continuously evaluates the network's state and adjusts constraint application to optimize the solution. This work addresses a critical challenge in quantum network design: the need for a self-optimizing system capable of handling the dynamic nature of quantum states. The proposed approach offers significant potential for advancing the practical application of quantum networks to tackle problems currently intractable for existing architectures.

title: String Quantum Computing for Non-Linear Geometric Optimization
abstract: String quantum computing (SQC) offers a fundamentally different approach to computation compared to traditional quantum computing, potentially unlocking new capabilities for optimization problems. This paper investigates the application of SQC to non-linear geometric optimization, a challenging area with significant potential for breakthroughs in fields like materials science, engineering design, and robotics. We propose a novel optimization algorithm leveraging SQC's inherent ability to represent and manipulate complex geometric structures, demonstrating its efficacy in solving specific optimization scenarios. The core mechanism centers around utilizing the quantum properties of the string to achieve a non-linear transformation, allowing the algorithm to navigate complex landscapes more effectively than classical methods. This paper will detail the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary results, highlighting the advantages and potential applications of SQC in this domain.

title: Adaptive High-Dimensional Continuous Space
abstract: This paper investigates the development of an adaptive high-dimensional continuous space algorithm designed to automatically adjust parameters in response to data distribution shifts. The core of the proposed approach is a novel self-adaptive learning algorithm that continuously monitors the data distribution and dynamically adjusts parameters to maximize model generalization. The algorithm's effectiveness stems from its ability to achieve parameter optimization without manual intervention, leading to improved model robustness and performance across a wide range of datasets. We present a detailed explanation of the algorithm's components, a methodology for parameter adjustment, and results demonstrating its performance gains compared to traditional approaches. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications and future directions of this technology.

title: Title: Probabilistic Quantum Error Mitigation via Adaptive Noise Injection
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionary advancements across diverse fields, but its inherent sensitivity to noise necessitates sophisticated error mitigation strategies. Current approaches often rely on fixed, computationally intensive noise injection schemes, limiting scalability and requiring substantial overhead. This paper introduces a novel probabilistic error mitigation strategy leveraging real-time monitoring of quantum circuit error characteristics to dynamically adjust noise injection levels. The algorithm, termed Adaptive Noise Injection (ANI), continuously assesses the error using a simplified error metric and adjusts the noise injection accordingly. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ANI through simulations and preliminary experiments, achieving significant error reduction compared to static mitigation methods while maintaining high accuracy. This research addresses a critical limitation in quantum error mitigation, paving the way for more efficient and practical quantum computations.

title: Quantum Information Entropy: A Theoretical Computation Framework
abstract: Quantum information entropy, a fundamental measure of uncertainty, is a complex concept that has long evaded direct computational analysis. This paper introduces a novel theoretical framework for calculating quantum information entropy, leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement and quantum algorithms to achieve precise and efficient computation. We present a new algorithm, the "Entangled Entropy Accelerator" (TEA), designed to exploit quantum entanglement to significantly accelerate entropy calculations compared to classical methods. The core mechanism of the TEA centers around the application of a tailored quantum algorithm to a specific type of quantum data, effectively reducing the computational complexity. The resultant framework offers a robust and scalable method for quantifying and analyzing quantum information entropy. This research demonstrates the potential of quantum computation to unlock new insights into the nature of information and its underlying dynamics.

Current optimization techniques frequently employ static representations, limiting the potential for finding truly innovative solutions. We propose a fractal-based method designed to automatically generate and adapt the problem space, enabling the discovery of complex patterns and ultimately, improved performance through dynamic constraint adjustment. The core mechanism centers around creating a self-consistent representation of the objective function, allowing the system to iteratively refine its approach to achieve a higher-quality solution. title: Temporal Graph Embeddings with Causal Reasoning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph embedding that explicitly incorporates temporal dynamics and causal reasoning. Traditional graph embeddings often treat nodes as static entities defined solely by their connections. However, real-world graphs evolve over time, and nodes are frequently influenced by causal relationships. This work addresses this limitation by developing a method that generates embeddings reflecting both the historical evolution of node features and inferred causal influences. We leverage a temporal sequence of node features and employ a causal inference module, such as Bayesian networks, to capture these relationships. The resulting embeddings aim to provide a more nuanced and potentially predictive representation of graph nodes, offering advantages in tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and anomaly detection. The core of the method lies in the integration of temporal information and causal reasoning, moving beyond purely structural representations of graphs.

title: 基于量子纠错码的分布式存储安全协议
abstract: This paper proposes a novel secure distributed storage protocol leveraging the principles of quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs). Traditional distributed storage systems face significant security vulnerabilities due to the inherent risks of data transmission and storage across multiple nodes. This protocol aims to mitigate these vulnerabilities by utilizing the inherent redundancy and error-correcting capabilities of QECCs. The core mechanism involves constructing a distributed storage system based on QECCs, ensuring data protection during both transmission and storage phases. The protocol's design addresses the limitations of conventional approaches, enhancing security and improving system reliability. Mathematical formulations and key concepts are presented to illustrate the protocol's operation and demonstrate its effectiveness. The key contributions lie in the efficient application of QECCs to a distributed storage environment, offering a robust solution against various attack vectors. Further research will focus on optimizing the protocol for large-scale deployments and exploring the integration with existing distributed storage technologies.

title: Quantum Entanglement Based on Non-symmetric Geometry: A Quantum Algorithm Design
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation and communication. This paper explores the development of a novel quantum algorithm leveraging non-symmetric geometry to achieve precise measurements and manipulations of quantum states, specifically tailored to optimize performance within a defined quantum system. We propose a new algorithmic framework that strategically utilizes entangled qubits to enhance the fidelity of quantum measurements and control, offering a potential pathway to enhanced computational capabilities. This research focuses on the integration of non-symmetric geometry to create a quantum algorithm that leverages the unique properties of entangled states, addressing a key challenge in the field of quantum computing. The core claim is that this approach will yield improved accuracy and efficiency in quantum state manipulation compared to existing algorithms.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning via Continuous Tensor Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning by representing symbolic knowledge as continuous tensor networks. Traditional neuro-symbolic systems often struggle with the disjointed nature of neural network pattern recognition and symbolic logic inference. Our method overcomes this challenge by allowing for a seamless transition between continuous and discrete reasoning. Neural networks are employed to learn the parameters within these tensor networks, effectively bridging the gap between perception and deduction. The core idea is to encode logical rules and relationships directly into the structure and parameters of a tensor network, allowing the system to perform both pattern recognition and logical inference. We demonstrate that this continuous representation facilitates more efficient and robust reasoning compared to conventional approaches. The system learns to manipulate the tensor network, effectively 'solving' logical problems by evolving its structure and parameter values. This approach offers a potential path towards more explainable and adaptable AI systems.

title: Probabilistic Relational Logic for Representing and Reasoning about Software Systems
abstract: This paper introduces Probabilistic Relational Logic (PRL), a novel formalism designed to address the limitations of traditional logic systems when dealing with the inherent uncertainty present in software systems. The core challenge in software engineering lies in accurately modeling the complex and often ambiguous relationships between software components, which are frequently subject to incomplete information, estimation errors, and evolving requirements. Conventional logical approaches often struggle to handle this uncertainty effectively. PRL overcomes this by extending relational logic with probability distributions, providing a means to represent the degree of belief associated with these uncertain relationships. The paper details the formal language of PRL, including its syntax and semantics, and outlines the probabilistic inference techniques employed for reasoning about system behavior. The core claim is that PRL offers a more suitable framework for representing and reasoning about software systems due to its ability to explicitly incorporate uncertainty, leading to more robust and reliable conclusions. The paper demonstrates the potential of PRL through a conceptual framework and highlights its applicability to various software engineering scenarios.

title: Meta-Learning for Domain Adaptation via Neural Architecture Search
abstract: Domain adaptation (DA) addresses the problem of transferring knowledge from a source domain with labeled data to a target domain with unlabeled data. A significant challenge in DA is the need for extensive hyperparameter tuning of the adaptation methods themselves, often involving manual selection of learning rates, regularization strengths, and other parameters. This work proposes a novel approach leveraging meta-learning and neural architecture search (NAS) to automate this process. Our core claim is that domain adaptation methods often require extensive hyperparameter tuning. We introduce a framework where NAS is integrated within a meta-learning framework, allowing the system to automatically discover optimal neural network architectures specifically tailored for adapting to new domains. This is guided by a meta-objective focused on minimizing the adaptation error. The proposed method effectively reduces the reliance on manual tuning, offering a more efficient and robust solution for domain adaptation. This paper outlines the architecture, training procedure, and experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Reinforcement Learning with Unknown Dynamics
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) traditionally relies on precise models of the environment, a requirement that often fails in real-world scenarios characterized by unknown or partially observable dynamics. This paper proposes a novel approach to address this challenge by integrating probabilistic programming with RL. We introduce a framework where the environment dynamics are explicitly modeled as probability distributions, allowing the RL agent to learn policies within a framework that inherently accounts for uncertainty. This approach enables the agent to not only optimize for expected rewards but also to reason about the likelihood of different outcomes, leading to more robust and adaptive behavior. The core of our method lies in using probabilistic programming to define a Bayesian model of the environment, where the dynamics are represented by probability distributions, and the agent learns a policy via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) or Variational Inference (VI) techniques. We demonstrate the efficacy of this framework through theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with simplified examples. The key contribution is the systematic approach to integrating probabilistic modeling and RL, providing a foundation for tackling complex RL problems with uncertain dynamics.

title: Multi-Scale Information Fusion and Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel multi-scale information fusion and optimization algorithm designed to address complex system optimization challenges. The core of the algorithm lies in its ability to simultaneously process information at various scales and facilitate optimal decision-making. We leverage a hierarchical perception neural network to decompose the problem into sub-problems of differing scales. A multi-scale attention mechanism then integrates information across these scales. Finally, a global optimization algorithm converges on the optimal solution. This approach overcomes the limitations of traditional optimization methods when dealing with multi-scale, heterogeneous data. The algorithm's architecture and operational principles are detailed, and its potential applications across various domains are discussed. The primary goal is to provide a robust and adaptable framework for tackling complex optimization problems where information is distributed across multiple resolutions.

title: Quantum Data Compression via Wavefunction Collapse
abstract: Quantum data compression aims to efficiently represent quantum states and information by exploiting the inherent fragility of quantum measurement processes. This paper explores a novel compression algorithm predicated on the principle of wavefunction collapse, hypothesizing that the collapse of a quantum wavefunction during compression provides a more efficient representation than traditional methods. We detail the core mechanism of this algorithm, outlining its design and the theoretical underpinning of its potential for near-lossless data compression. The paper presents a detailed explanation of the algorithm's components, including the analysis of the waveform, the collapse process, and the reconstruction process. We discuss the potential advantages and challenges associated with this approach, ultimately asserting that it represents a significant step towards a more robust and efficient data compression paradigm.

title: From Process Loss to Assembly Bonus: Human-Grounded Diagnosis of Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration
abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used for collaborative problem solving and human-group simulation. This makes outcome-only evaluation insufficient: if LLM groups are used as models of human groups, we need to know whether they succeed or fail through human-like deliberative mechanisms. We compare human group chats with matched LLM deliberation traces on Wason-style deductive reasoning, then test whether the same process signatures generalize to analogical, abductive, and analytical tasks. Humans and LLMs show the same assembly bonus asymmetry: discussion improves the average member more often than the best initial member. Initial-answer diversity accounts for the effect of model heterogeneity, increasing movement in both corrective and destructive directions. The main differences are process-level. Compared with humans, LLM groups follow majorities more often, surface less unique information, and converge earlier; correct minority signals succeed mainly when re-expressed early. Interventions motivated by human group-decision research yield modest improvements in collective outcomes, but do not remove the coordination bottleneck. Together, these results suggest that LLM groups can reproduce some outcome-level patterns of human deliberation while diverging in the mechanisms that generate assembly bonus and process loss, with implications for group simulation and human-AI collaboration.

title: BIGREASONS/Latent_Planning: LatentBench v1.0.0
abstract: Latent reasoning seeks to perform intermediate computation directly in the hidden-state space of a language model, potentially reducing the need for repeated autoregressive decoding. However, evaluating whether a predicted latent state represents the correct next reasoning state remains challenging. Standard geometric objectives such as cosine similarity or mean-squared error measure proximity in representation space, but proximity alone does not establish semantic correctness. We introduce LatentBench, a framework for evaluating semantic fidelity in latent transition models using a frozen language-model teacher, task-level representation probes, oracle transitions, and action-control ablations. The framework separates geometric reconstruction from semantic state advancement through Semantic Gain and Oracle Gap, while simultaneously tracking cosine similarity, mean-centered cosine similarity, mean-squared error, and probe accuracy. We evaluate Linear, MLP, and Transformer transition models on the Countdown task using a frozen TinyLlama teacher, with three independent seeds per architecture. Across the nine audited experimental conditions, all three architectures exhibit consistently non-zero Oracle Gaps while maintaining high raw cosine similarity. Mean Oracle Gap is 0.1944 for Linear, 0.1789 for MLP, and 0.1860 for Transformer. All nine audited runs produced negative True Action Semantic Gain, indicating limited semantic advancement despite strong geometric proximity to the current representation. A Welch's ANOVA does not detect a statistically significant architecture effect on Oracle Gap (F(2,3.59)=1.160, p=0.409). Pairwise Welch tests with Holm correction likewise do not reach statistical significance. Because only three seeds are available per architecture, these results should be interpreted as inconclusive with respect to fine-grained architectural differences rather than as evidence of equivalence. Our results demonstrate that, in the evaluated Countdown and TinyLlama setting, geometric similarity alone can substantially overstate the semantic fidelity of latent transitions. The findings motivate evaluation protocols that explicitly measure task-relevant semantic state preservation rather than relying solely on representation-level reconstruction metrics.

title: HOLD: A GENERAL FRAMEWORK FOR GUARDED PRESERVATION OF PARTIAL OPERATIONS
abstract: Partial operations arise whenever an otherwise meaningful operation excludes particular inputs, such as division or remainder with a zero divisor. This note introduces a guarded preservation framework in which a partial operation is extended by an explicitly specified state-preservation branch. We define the primitive zero-recipient operator HOLD: X × {0} → X by HOLD(x,0) = x, understood as IX(x). More generally, for any operation A: X × N+ → X defined on positive counts, the guarded extension F: X × N → X is defined by F(x,0)=x and F(x,n)=A(x,n) for n>0. Main results: Guarded Extension Theorem (Totality): F is total and agrees with A on its original domain. Uniqueness: F is the unique extension satisfying the prescribed zero-branch condition P(x). Stability and Compositional Closure: Identity preservation is stable under repetition and composition. Crucially, the framework does not redefine x/0 or x mod 0 as arithmetic values. x/0 remains undefined. HOLD is a separate semantic policy for systems whose specified behavior at a guard state is preservation (e.g., zero-recipient allocation). This work formalizes a common operational pattern and provides a precise vocabulary for separating arithmetic partiality from deliberate operational policy. title: Adaptive Topological Structure Networks: An Automated Self-Organizing Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive topological structure network (ATSN) algorithm designed for automated self-organization learning. Traditional approaches often rely on manual topology design, limiting the algorithm's ability to learn and adjust network structure. Our proposed algorithm leverages the principles of topology to construct a node network with inherent self-organization capabilities, enabling it to learn and refine the network topology through interactions. The algorithm's core mechanism involves constructing a node network with a dynamically evolving topology, driven by feedback loops and interactions, ultimately enhancing data representation. This approach offers a novel and automated method for learning complex data patterns, surpassing the limitations of conventional topology-based methods.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Aggregation
abstract: Quantum entanglement information aggregation is a novel theoretical framework exploring the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement with classical information to achieve quantum information aggregation. This paper investigates a proposed quantum data compression and transmission method that utilizes entanglement to enhance data transfer efficiency. We introduce a quantum information passing mechanism based on entanglement, employing entanglement for encoding and decoding, and propose a quantum data compression algorithm that leverages entanglement's properties. The research aims to demonstrate the potential of quantum entanglement in revolutionizing information transfer paradigms.

title: Korpus Paralel Dwibahasa Indonesia–Jawa: Dataset Terjemahan Kalimat Lintas Domain
abstract: Korpus paralel dwibahasa yang dirancang secara sistematis untuk mendukung kajian linguistik, penerjemahan berbasis mesin (machine translation), serta pemrosesan bahasa alami (Natural Language Processing / NLP) antara bahasa Indonesia dan bahasa Jawa. title: The title: Topological Genetic Algorithm for Enhanced Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel application of the Topological Genetic Algorithm (TGAE) to complex systems, leveraging the inherent topological structure to optimize system stability, efficiency, and performance. We explore how incorporating topological features into the search process can significantly improve the algorithm's effectiveness in challenging scenarios. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically adjusting search spaces based on topological relationships, offering a powerful approach to address the limitations of traditional optimization techniques. This work aims to broaden the applicability of TGAE beyond simple optimization problems, demonstrating its potential for complex system design and control.

title: Nonlinear Matrix Decomposition Quantum Simulation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum simulation, focusing on the non-linear matrix decomposition algorithm. The core claim is that this algorithm, leveraging quantum entanglement, offers a significantly more accurate and efficient simulation of complex quantum systems, particularly those involving quantum entanglement and quantum field effects. Traditional matrix decomposition methods often suffer from errors, and this work introduces a quantum-based technique designed to exploit the unique properties of quantum entanglement to enhance simulation fidelity. The algorithm's mechanism centers on establishing and manipulating entangled states to extract critical physical parameters and facilitate accurate simulation. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary results, demonstrating its potential for advanced quantum system modeling.

title: Non-linear Fourier Transform for Quantum Computing Constraint Optimization
abstract: Quantum computing offers unprecedented computational power, but designing efficient quantum algorithms remains a significant challenge. Constraint optimization, a crucial step in many quantum algorithms, often requires complex and computationally expensive optimization strategies. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing non-linear Fourier transform (NLFT) to address this challenge. We develop a quantum algorithm that leverages the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to efficiently solve constraint optimization problems. The core mechanism centers around encoding the objective function and constraints within a quantum state, enabling a direct and effective optimization process. The proposed algorithm demonstrates superior performance compared to traditional methods, particularly for problems exhibiting strong entanglement and complex constraints.

title: Dynamic Graph Neural Networks with Contextual Memory Encoding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) that addresses a critical limitation of traditional GNNs – their inability to effectively model the dynamic evolution of graph structures. We propose Dynamic Graph Neural Networks with Contextual Memory Encoding (DGMNE), a framework that integrates a contextual memory component to explicitly capture and adapt to the temporal changes within a graph. The core idea is to augment standard GNN layers with a separate memory module. This module stores embeddings representing past graph states, weighted according to their temporal proximity and relevance. The weighting scheme allows the network to learn and dynamically update its understanding of the graph's topology based on its historical evolution. This approach significantly improves the representation learning capabilities of GNNs, leading to enhanced performance in tasks where graph dynamics are paramount. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DGMNE through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components and operational principles. The proposed architecture offers a flexible and powerful method for incorporating temporal information into GNNs, opening up new avenues for research and applications.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Systems for Formal Verification of Concurrent Programs
abstract: Formal verification of concurrent programs remains a significant challenge due to the inherent complexity of managing interactions and potential race conditions. This work proposes a novel approach utilizing neuro-symbolic systems to bridge the gap between traditional formal verification methods and the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks. The system combines a neural network tasked with representing program states and behaviors with a symbolic theorem prover for rigorous property verification. The core mechanism involves the neural network learning a compact representation of the concurrent program's dynamics, which is then leveraged by the theorem prover to formally prove properties such as mutual exclusion, deadlock freedom, and progress. This approach offers a more scalable and robust solution compared to purely symbolic or purely neural methods by capitalizing on the strengths of both paradigms. The system's architecture and integration strategy are presented, highlighting the key components and their interactions. The potential of this integrated approach for tackling complex concurrent program verification problems is explored, with a focus on improving verification efficiency and expanding the scope of verifiable properties. Finally, the system's performance is evaluated through a theoretical analysis and illustrative examples, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying critical concurrency issues.

title: Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning with Temporal Context
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to self-supervised learning, termed Contrastive Learning with Temporal Context (CLTC), designed to overcome the limitations of traditional contrastive learning methods when applied to dynamic environments. We argue that standard contrastive learning struggles to effectively learn robust representations when data exhibits temporal dependencies. Our core idea is to augment contrastive learning by incorporating temporal context – comparing representations of a node at different points in time. This is achieved through a learned temporal embedding that captures the evolving features associated with each node. We formulate the learning objective as a contrastive loss that encourages similar representations for temporally aligned nodes and dissimilar representations for temporally mismatched nodes, all within the framework of a contrastive learning paradigm. The key contribution of this work lies in explicitly modelling the temporal dimension, leading to representations that are more sensitive to changes in the underlying data distribution. We demonstrate the effectiveness of CLTC through a theoretical analysis and provide a conceptual framework for its implementation.

title: Time-like Embeddings and Causal Inference
abstract: This paper explores the potential of time-like embeddings for causal inference. We propose a framework that leverages manifold learning techniques to represent time series data within a high-dimensional time-like space. By analyzing the geometric properties of this space, specifically utilizing concepts from tangent space analysis, we aim to uncover latent causal relationships within the data. Unlike traditional causal inference methods that often rely on manually constructed causal models, our approach offers an automated means of discovering causal patterns directly from the data. This work lays the groundwork for a novel approach to causal discovery by integrating the power of manifold learning with fundamental geometric insights. The core claim is that embedding time series data into a time-like manifold space can reveal underlying causal relationships. The key mechanism involves mapping time series data to a high-dimensional manifold space using manifold learning algorithms and leveraging the manifold's geometric properties, such as the tangent space, to analyze relationships between data points and, consequently, infer causal relationships. ---

title: Adaptive Quantum Path Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive quantum path optimization algorithm designed to enhance the efficiency of quantum information transmission and processing, particularly in long-distance quantum communication and quantum computing. Traditional approaches often rely on probabilistic methods, while this algorithm leverages geometric properties of quantum paths to provide superior optimization capabilities. The core mechanism centers around intelligently adjusting the path's shape to maximize fidelity and minimize error propagation, offering a significant advancement in this crucial area of quantum technology. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulations and preliminary experiments.

title: Adaptive Topological Transformation of Quantum Entanglement
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, offers unparalleled potential for secure communication and computation. However, harnessing this intricate phenomenon presents significant challenges in terms of information storage and transfer. This paper explores the transformative potential of adaptive topological transformations, proposing a novel algorithm to dynamically reshape quantum entanglement, ultimately enabling more efficient data storage and transmission. The core claim centers on the ability to self-reconfigure quantum entanglement, a capability that surpasses the limitations of traditional approaches. We delve into the underlying mechanisms and propose a theoretical framework for this transformative process, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize quantum information processing.

title: Adaptive Graph Embedding with Relational Contextualization
abstract: Graph embedding techniques have become indispensable for representing and analyzing complex networks. However, traditional methods often struggle to effectively capture the intricate relationships and contextual nuances present in real-world graphs. This paper introduces a novel adaptive graph embedding approach that integrates relational contextualization. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts node embeddings by considering the types of connections and associated attributes of neighboring nodes. This contextual awareness allows for the creation of more accurate and informative node representations, ultimately improving performance in downstream graph-based tasks. The core of our method lies in a learned weighting system that prioritizes the influence of different contextual factors, leading to a robust and adaptable embedding process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and illustrate its advantages using a simplified illustrative example. The key innovation is the adaptive weighting scheme, allowing the model to prioritize relevant contextual information during the embedding process, leading to more nuanced and accurate node representations. ---

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Adaptive Rule Extraction
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning, termed adaptive rule extraction. The core idea is to synergistically combine the strengths of neural networks and symbolic reasoning systems. Specifically, we propose a system where a neural network learns to automatically generate symbolic rules from data. These rules are then employed for logical inference. Crucially, the neural network continuously adapts and refines these rules based on the outcomes of the reasoning process. This iterative process allows the system to evolve its understanding of the domain and improve its reasoning performance over time. We demonstrate the potential of this adaptive approach through a theoretical framework and outline a system architecture. The system's ability to dynamically adjust rules represents a significant advance over static rule-based systems and traditional neural network approaches, offering increased flexibility and robustness. The framework addresses challenges inherent in both purely symbolic and purely neural reasoning, creating a more powerful and adaptable reasoning engine. The system's performance is evaluated conceptually, highlighting the benefits of the adaptive rule extraction mechanism.

title: Self-Referential Kernel Learning for Semantic Representation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to semantic representation learning within the framework of kernel methods, termed "Self-Referential Kernel Learning." The core idea is to allow the kernel itself to learn from its outputs, creating a self-referential feedback loop. Traditional kernel methods often rely on manually designed kernels, which can be suboptimal for complex semantic relationships. Our algorithm dynamically updates the kernel's parameters based on the similarity scores it calculates, effectively learning a representation that better captures semantic similarities. We formalize this process with a specific learning objective and optimization strategy. The key contribution is the introduction of this iterative self-adaptation mechanism, which we hypothesize will lead to significantly improved semantic representation learning compared to conventional kernel methods. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach and outline a potential implementation strategy, highlighting the advantages and potential challenges associated with this novel technique. The overall goal is to develop a more flexible and adaptive kernel method capable of capturing nuanced semantic information. ---

title: Brand relationships in conversation: a review of conversational agents using bibliometrics and language models
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to synthesise research on conversational agents in the context of brand relationships to map the current state of knowledge, propose an integrative framework and develop a future research agenda. Design/methodology/approach This study analyses 293 publications from Scopus and Web of Science (2004–2025), combining bibliometric analysis, topic modelling and a multi-step validation protocol based on embedding analysis and expert consensus. Findings Five thematic clusters explain how conversational agents shape brand relationships through functional competence, social simulation, anthropomorphic projection, technological affordances and emotional resonance. An integrative framework structures these findings into an explanatory model linking configurable design features, psychological mediators and brand relationship outcomes. The current boundaries of knowledge are defined by three key tensions: the anthropomorphism paradox, the stage-contingency problem and the intensity asymmetry between positive and negative outcomes. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is among the first reviews to examine conversational agent research through the brand relationship perspective, combining bibliometric mapping with language-model topic modelling and expert validation. The proposed framework bridges descriptive synthesis and mechanism-based modelling, and the expert validation protocol helps address the subjectivity concerns associated with traditional literature reviews.

title: Probability Inference: A Dynamic Probabilistic Model
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic inference framework, termed a Dynamic Probabilistic Model (DPM), designed to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of inference processes. Traditional probabilistic models often rely on static, pre-defined parameters, limiting their adaptability to complex data. The DPM addresses this limitation by dynamically adjusting the model parameters based on incoming data, enabling a more responsive and effective inference strategy. We explore the core mechanism behind this adaptation, detailing how the model's parameters are refined in real-time to optimize performance. This work introduces a new approach to probabilistic inference, offering a potential advancement over existing methods, particularly in scenarios involving dynamic data and high-dimensional input spaces.

title: Title: Zero-Assisted Quantum Simulation of Dynamical Systems
abstract: Quantum simulation of complex dynamical systems holds immense potential for understanding and modeling natural phenomena. However, the computational demands of these simulations often limit their practical application. This paper introduces a novel zero-assisted quantum simulation technique designed to significantly reduce computational costs while maintaining high fidelity. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a rigorous analysis of its impact on simulation accuracy and scalability. The core mechanism involves systematically minimizing the influence of quantum fluctuations on the simulation, offering a pathway towards more efficient and accessible quantum simulations. The resulting approach promises to accelerate the study of dynamic systems and unlock new possibilities in diverse fields.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Geometric Chaos Simulation
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm for the accurate simulation of complex geometric chaos systems. Geometric chaos, characterized by intricate, self-repeating patterns, poses a significant challenge for traditional computational methods. Quantum mechanics offers potential advantages in representing and manipulating these patterns, and this work explores the application of quantum algorithms to achieve a more precise and efficient simulation of such systems. We introduce a quantum framework designed to explore the dynamics of such systems, utilizing principles of quantum superposition and entanglement to enhance the representation of chaotic states. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through simulations of a specific, highly complex geometric chaos system, showcasing improvements in accuracy and computational efficiency compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers on exploiting quantum entanglement to represent and propagate chaotic states, leading to a more robust and nuanced simulation of the system's behavior.

title: Algorithmic Fairness via Differential Privacy with Group-Awareness
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to algorithmic fairness by integrating differential privacy (DP) with group-awareness. Traditional differential privacy mechanisms, while effective in protecting individual privacy, often fail to address biases that can arise when algorithms are applied across different demographic groups, leading to disparate impact. We introduce a modified differential privacy framework that explicitly considers these group-based disparities. The core idea is to adjust privacy parameters—specifically, the privacy budget (ε, δ)—to balance privacy protection with fairness objectives. Our approach aims to mitigate biases by tailoring the level of privacy protection to the sensitivity of the data and the potential for unfair outcomes within specific groups. We demonstrate, theoretically and conceptually, how this group-aware DP framework can significantly improve fairness outcomes compared to standard DP, offering a practical pathway towards building more equitable algorithms. The central contribution lies in the systematic method for calibrating the privacy budget to account for group-specific vulnerabilities and sensitivities. This work lays the groundwork for a more nuanced and robust understanding of how to combine DP and fairness in real-world applications.

title: Dynamic Topological Embedded Knowledge Graph Reasoning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to knowledge graph reasoning, termed "Dynamic Topological Embedded Knowledge Graph Reasoning." The core claim is that knowledge graph structures – including relationships and node attributes – can be dynamically embedded into neural network architectures through real-time learning and adaptation, leading to improved inference efficiency and accuracy. This is achieved through a "topological embedding" method that maps knowledge graph connections to neural network connection weights, optimized using reinforcement learning to reflect the structure of the knowledge graph. Existing methods often treat knowledge graphs as static inputs to neural networks, neglecting their dynamic characteristics and lacking effective learning mechanisms. Our approach addresses this limitation by creating a self-adapting system that continuously learns and evolves alongside the knowledge graph, ultimately providing a more robust and accurate reasoning capability. The proposed method demonstrates the potential for significant improvements in knowledge graph reasoning tasks compared to traditional static embedding approaches.

title: Self-Adaptive Topology Quantum Simulation Dynamic Topology Adjustment
abstract: This paper investigates the application of self-adaptive topology in quantum simulation to dynamically adjust the underlying topology of quantum systems, enabling more accurate and efficient simulation of quantum information storage. Traditional quantum simulation methods often rely on static parameterizations, limiting their ability to capture the intricate dynamics of quantum systems. We propose a novel framework where the topology of the quantum system is actively modified during the simulation process, guided by computational algorithms. This dynamic adjustment allows for a more comprehensive representation of the system's evolution and facilitates the prediction of quantum information storage efficiency. The core mechanism involves the iterative refinement of the quantum state representation, driven by the algorithm's output, to achieve a higher fidelity simulation.

title: Topological Entanglement-Based Codes for Quantum Information Transmission
abstract: This paper investigates the construction and properties of topological entanglement-based codes for quantum information transmission. Traditional quantum error correction codes face significant challenges in mitigating channel losses and decoherence, particularly over long distances. We propose a novel approach utilizing the inherent topological properties of entangled states to enhance error correction efficiency. The core concept involves leveraging entanglement as the fundamental resource for the code, employing carefully designed entanglement networks and encoding schemes to achieve robust error detection and correction. Our framework offers a potential pathway to overcoming limitations inherent in conventional quantum error correction, promising improved performance in long-distance quantum communication. The theoretical analysis presented herein establishes a foundation for future research and development in this area.

title: Title: Universal Quantum State Reconstruction Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents the development of a Universal Quantum State Reconstruction Algorithm (UQSRA) designed to reconstruct complete quantum states from a single measurement, irrespective of the measurement type or initial state. The algorithm leverages a novel quantum state reconstruction technique centered around probabilistic collapse and entanglement manipulation, offering a potential paradigm shift in quantum state processing. We outline the core mechanism, detailing the algorithm's operational steps and the underlying principles driving its capabilities. The significance of this work lies in its potential to overcome limitations in existing quantum state manipulation techniques, opening doors to novel applications within quantum information processing and quantum cryptography.

title: Formal Verification of Adaptive Program Generation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to software development leveraging the power of formal verification and adaptive program generation. The core idea is to create a closed-loop system where formal verification guarantees the correctness of generated programs, while adaptive optimization algorithms continuously refine their performance. We introduce a framework that utilizes techniques like model checking and theorem proving to establish the validity of a program against a given specification. The verification results then drive a program generator, producing an initial program conforming to the specification. Subsequently, an adaptive optimization algorithm analyzes the generated program's performance and autonomously modifies its structure to enhance efficiency. This process is iterative, continuously improving both the correctness and the performance of the program. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of these two approaches, offering a robust and efficient method for software development, particularly in domains demanding high reliability and performance. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this framework and discuss its potential applications, outlining a path toward automated and trustworthy software creation.

title: Metaheuristic-driven automatic ARIMA order selection using spider monkey optimization for agricultural production forecasting
abstract: The Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model requires appropriate selection of autoregressive (p), differencing (d), and moving average (q) orders for accurate forecasting. Conventional order selection methods, such as grid search and stepwise information-criterion approaches, can be computationally expensive and prone to suboptimal solutions. This study proposes ARIMA-Spider Monkey Optimization (ARIMA-SMO), an automated framework that employs Spider Monkey Optimization to identify optimal ARIMA orders. In the proposed approach, each spider monkey represents a candidate ARIMA (p,d,q) configuration, and model fitness is evaluated using a combination of statistical goodness-of-fit and forecasting accuracy. The local and global leader mechanisms, together with adaptive subgroup restructuring, balance exploration and exploitation of the search space. The method was evaluated using agricultural production time series from India and compared with Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Bayesian Optimization (BO)-based ARIMA models. Across all six-production series, ARIMA-SMO consistently achieved the lowest forecasting errors while requiring less computational time than the competing approaches. For the total food grains series, ARIMA-SMO reduced the test RMSE to 35.75 compared with 43.96 (GA), 39.84 (PSO), and 37.12 (BO). The results demonstrate that ARIMA-SMO is an effective and computationally efficient framework for automatic ARIMA order selection and time-series forecasting.
