title: Optimizing ASTER and PRISMA data for lithological mapping and mineral detection in NW Pakistan
abstract: Remote sensing is a fundamental tool in mineral exploration and lithological mapping. The northern mountainous belt of Pakistan has significant mineral deposits, although hyperspectral data remain underutilized in this region. This study applied an integrated techniques, including principal component analysis (PCA), independent component analysis (ICA), minimum noise fraction (MNF), spectral angle mapper (SAM), mahalanobis distance (MD), spectral index (SI) and support vector machine (SVM) to ASTER and PRISMA data for mapping lithological units and alteration zones in the Garam Chashma region of northwest Pakistan. These approaches successfully isolated target signals, delineated lithological units and mineralization zones, and demonstrated a strong spatial correlation with ground observations and known Cu-Fe mineralization. Field validations and laboratory analysis confirm the remote sensing results and additional identified potential areas near Garam Chashma town, including Momi village, along Arkari Gol and west of the Drunil area. The results supports the reliability of the adopted methodology for minerals exploration globally.

title: A Bayesian-optimized CNN-GRU framework for multimodal short-term solar photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: The integration of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems into the energy grid presents several challenges for controlling energy systems, primarily due to their intermittent nature. To manage this intermittency, accurate short-term forecasts are required. This study proposes a Bayesian-optimized sequence-aligned hybrid Convolutional Neural Network and Gated Recurrent Unit (CNN–GRU) framework to predict PV power 15 min ahead using multimodal sky images ( 6 4 × 6 4 × 4 8 ) and historical PV time-series data (16 × 1). Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) optimization with Hyperband pruning is employed to systematically search the hyperparameter space. On a standardized 1-year benchmark dataset, the proposed model achieves an overall Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 2 . 4 1 9 k W , a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1 . 1 5 3 k W , and a Forecast Skill (FS) of 18.96%. These results demonstrate a 3.36% improvement in RMSE, a 7.83% improvement in MAE, and a 17.40% relative improvement in Forecast Skill compared to the state-of-the-art (SOTA) model, while achieving an 80.0% reduction in model parameters.

title: LASSNet: Level-Aware Availability-Conditioned Spatial-Semantic Fusion for Brain Tumor Segmentation with Missing MRI Modalities
abstract: Brain tumor segmentation from multimodal MRI relies on complementary evidence across four imaging sequences, yet one or more modalities may be unavailable because of acquisition cost, protocol variation, scan failure, or patient condition. Existing work has explored reconstruction, knowledge transfer, and direct feature fusion, but leaves open whether missing-modality fusion should change with representation level. High-resolution lateral features retain spatial detail, whereas compressed bottleneck features encode semantic and inter-modality context. We therefore hypothesize that fusion should be conditioned jointly on modality availability and feature hierarchy. We propose the Level-Aware Availability-Conditioned Spatial-Semantic Fusion Network (LASSNet), which contains two level-specialized modules. Hierarchical Availability-Conditioned Fusion (HACF) constructs four lateral representations using count-normalized aggregation of available modalities, mask-conditioned channel modulation, and local 3D refinement. Tri-Scale Relational-Spatial Fusion (TriRSF) models relations among available modality descriptors and spatial context across multiple bottleneck resolutions, followed by cross-scale aggregation and availability-conditioned global spatial attention. A shared coarse-to-fine decoder starts from TriRSF semantics and progressively injects HACF features, without reconstructing missing inputs. Across all 15 non-empty modality configurations, LASSNet obtains mean Dice scores of 76.7% and 83.2% over WT, TC, and ET on BraTS2019 and BraTS2023, respectively.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习的自然语言处理
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive machine learning to natural language processing (NLP), focusing on enhancing the understanding and generation capabilities of language models. Traditional NLP systems often rely on static models, limiting their ability to adapt to diverse text inputs. We propose a novel framework leveraging adaptive mechanisms to dynamically adjust model parameters based on text features. This approach allows the model to learn optimal representations and representations, leading to improved performance across various NLP tasks. The core mechanism utilizes a self-tuning parameter adjustment process, iteratively refining the model's internal state to achieve higher accuracy and fluency. The research explores the benefits of this dynamic adaptation and demonstrates its efficacy through several benchmark experiments. We conclude by highlighting the potential of this approach to advance the state-of-the-art in NLP.

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Branching in Genetic Algorithms
abstract: Genetic algorithms (GAs) have proven to be a powerful tool for optimization problems across various fields. However, traditional implementations often struggle with convergence issues, particularly in complex search spaces. This paper introduces a novel branching strategy for GAs that leverages non-Euclidean topology, aiming to enhance both the efficiency and robustness of the algorithms. We propose a branching mechanism that dynamically adjusts the branching points based on the evolutionary trajectory, leading to more flexible and adaptable solutions. The core mechanism centers around a hierarchical branching structure that avoids premature convergence and encourages exploration of diverse regions of the search space. This approach is rigorously analyzed and demonstrates improved performance on benchmark problems, particularly in situations exhibiting complex, non-linear relationships.

title: Title: Adaptive Complexity Curves in Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the integration of adaptive complexity curves within evolutionary algorithms to enhance robustness and mitigate premature convergence. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often struggle with local optima, necessitating careful parameter tuning and potentially lengthy search times. We propose a novel mechanism that dynamically adjusts the search space based on a 'complexity curve' – a visual representation of the system's internal state and observed patterns – allowing the algorithm to intelligently navigate complex landscapes. This approach aims to promote greater exploration and ultimately lead to more effective solutions. The core of our design lies in monitoring the system's internal state and adjusting the search space to avoid getting trapped in suboptimal regions of the search space. We present a theoretical framework for the complexity curve and demonstrate its effectiveness through a series of simulations focusing on a specific optimization problem.

title: FADE-RIPE: A Robust Quantum Optimal Control Algorithm for Superconducting Transmons with Realistic Hardware Constraints (reference implementation)
abstract: FADE-RIPE: Transmon Quantum-Gate Optimizer FADE-RIPE (Fidelity Aware, Distortion-aware, Environment-conscious Robust Iterative Pulse Engineering) is a gradient-based quantum optimal control method for a single-qubit gate on a 4-level (N=4) transmon, benchmarked against GRAPE and CRAB (via qutip_qtrl). The model and optimizer include: Realistic transmon physics: An N=4 Hilbert space with Kerr/anharmonic H0, a subspace-projected 2x2 target gate, and an explicit penalty for population leaking into levels |2>, |3>. Exact Lindbladian propagation and gradient: Piecewise-constant Lindblad master-equation propagation with an exact analytic gradient (via the augmented-generator/Frechet-derivative trick). AWG bandwidth filter: A Butterworth low-pass filter on the control pulses, represented as an exact linear operator so the gradient chain rule through it is exact. Filter-function noise penalty: A numerical filter function F(omega) of the optimized pulse, penalized against a 1/f (flux) or thermal-photon power spectral density via an overlap integral. Thermal initial-state fidelity: As-built fidelity optimizations starting from a Boltzmann-weighted thermal state rather than the pure ground state. This upload contains the reference implementation fade_realistic.py, which includes the physics model, optimizer, baseline comparisons, and the analysis/plotting pipeline used for the simulations reported in the companion paper.

title: Title: Self-Assembling Topological Networks for Data Compression
abstract: This paper explores the application of self-assembling topological networks to data compression, offering a novel approach that leverages the inherent structure of topological spaces to achieve efficient data representation. Traditional compression methods often require complex algorithms and significant computational resources. This work proposes a fundamentally different strategy: dynamically adjusting the connectivity of a network based on the data's characteristics, effectively creating a self-organizing structure. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, highlighting its potential for improved compression rates and reduced computational overhead compared to conventional methods. The core of our design involves the creation of a topology that adapts to the data, leading to a more robust and adaptable compression technique.

title: ##拓扑映射的自适应量子纠缠生成
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum information, is crucial for secure communication and powerful quantum computation. Traditional methods of generating entanglement often rely on complex, pre-defined protocols. This paper proposes a novel quantum entanglement generation algorithm based on the robust and adaptable properties of topological mappings. We develop a system that dynamically adjusts the mapping parameters to generate entangled states tailored to the evolving quantum state. The core mechanism leverages the inherent topological structure of mappings to create entanglement without requiring explicit manipulation of the underlying quantum states. This approach offers a promising pathway towards efficient and adaptable quantum entanglement generation, potentially revolutionizing quantum communication and computation. We detail the algorithm's architecture, key mathematical formulations, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Title: Universal Prime Number Generation via Quantum Simulation (UPQGS)
abstract: The generation of prime numbers has historically relied on deterministic algorithms, limiting their security against brute-force attacks. This paper introduces Universal Prime Number Generation via Quantum Simulation (UPQGS), a novel quantum algorithm designed to produce prime numbers with a guaranteed level of randomness and enhanced security. We propose a quantum simulation approach that leverages the inherent properties of quantum mechanics to explore the prime number space in a statistically diverse manner. The core mechanism centers on utilizing a quantum algorithm to simulate the evolution of a prime number generator, generating a statistically representative set of prime numbers. This approach promises to provide a fundamentally new method for cryptographic security, surpassing the limitations of traditional prime number generation techniques. The research will detail the quantum algorithm, its implementation, and the resulting characteristics of the generated prime numbers, emphasizing the algorithm's ability to achieve a high degree of randomness and statistical diversity.

abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of quantum algorithms by leveraging the principles of causal inference. Traditional quantum algorithm optimization often relies on heuristic methods or black-box approaches, lacking the transparency and robustness required for complex systems. We propose a novel framework that integrates causal inference with quantum algorithm design, aiming to identify and mitigate critical factors influencing algorithm performance. The core of our approach involves constructing a causal model of the quantum algorithm, represented as a causal Bayesian network. This network allows us to explicitly model dependencies between algorithmic components, enabling targeted interventions to improve efficiency and accuracy. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical analysis, outlining a methodology for identifying confounding variables and implementing causal interventions. The resulting framework offers a more interpretable and reliable path towards optimizing quantum algorithms, particularly in scenarios where understanding underlying causal relationships is paramount.

title: Quantum Algorithm Optimization Based on the Many-Worlds Interpretation
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization by leveraging the Many-Worlds Interpretation (MWI) of quantum mechanics. We propose a quantum algorithm design where the algorithm operates in a superposition of universes, enabling intermittent interactions and enhanced search efficiency. The algorithm utilizes the inherent probabilistic nature of MWI to explore a vast computational space concurrently, potentially overcoming limitations faced by standard quantum algorithms. This research introduces a new paradigm for quantum algorithm optimization, moving beyond traditional methods by embracing the multi-universal perspective. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and algorithmic design, highlighting its potential to significantly improve the speed and efficiency of quantum optimization processes. Further research will focus on developing specific implementations and evaluating the algorithm's performance against established quantum optimization techniques. ---

title: LLM-Extracted Temporal Hypergraphs for Modeling Disease Severity and Clinical Trajectories From Clinical Documents (Preprint)
abstract: BACKGROUND Clinical trajectory modeling requires representations of how multiple clinical dimensions interact and evolve over time. Conventional knowledge graphs are limited to pairwise edges and therefore cannot natively represent the higher-order interactions that characterize clinical events, in which patient factors, findings, treatments, and severity co-occur. No integrated framework combines large language model (LLM)-driven structured extraction from unstructured clinical documents with temporal hypergraph construction for trajectory modeling. OBJECTIVE We aimed to develop and validate a four-dimensional (4D) temporal hypergraph framework (4D-HyperGraph) that unifies patient history, clinical evidence, treatment trajectory, and dynamic severity in a single representation for clinical trajectory modeling. METHODS Four-dimensional clinical information was extracted from eight types of unstructured Chinese clinical documents for a retrospective cohort of 251 patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD; stable, n=54; acute exacerbation, n=88; exacerbation with infection, n=109), using a two-stage deidentification pipeline and LLM-driven extraction with dimension-specific prompts. Hyperedges were typed by dimension and assembled into a temporal hypergraph with HyperGraphRAG. A hypergraph neural network (HyperGNN) with dimension-level and temporal attention was trained for three-way classification, exacerbation prediction, and severity regression against a clinical severity composite score (CSCS). Five baselines were compared under stratified 5-fold cross-validation across 3 seeds, with dimension-level ablation, a temporally disjoint hold-out split, and external validation at a second hospital. RESULTS For three-way classification, 4D-HyperGraph with an XGBoost readout (4D-XGB) reached a 3-seed mean macro-averaged F1 of 0.615 (SD 0.010; 95% CI 0.580–0.653) versus 0.427 (SD 0.008) for the structured-feature XGBoost baseline, and 0.550 (SD 0.012) versus 0.436 (SD 0.017) on the temporally disjoint split. Exacerbation prediction reached a 3-seed mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.711 (SD 0.013) internally but 0.695 (SD 0.015) on the temporal split, below the structured baseline (0.715, SD 0.009). Externally, a balanced cohort (n=87) yielded an AUC-ROC of 0.865 versus 0.822 for the baseline, whereas external three-way classification stayed below baseline (macro-F1 0.449 vs 0.484; 0.441 vs 0.467 in a label-quality sensitivity analysis). For severity regression, the end-to-end HyperGNN achieved R2=0.216 and Pearson r=0.575, the highest among the deep-learning architectures; removing the severity dimension produced the largest ablation effect (r declined by 20.7%). No comparison survived Bonferroni correction (5 baselines × 3 tasks; corrected α=.003); the differences are indicative rather than confirmatory. CONCLUSIONS 4D-HyperGraph provides a general approach—designed to be disease-agnostic—for constructing temporal hypergraphs from unstructured clinical documents. Its primary contribution is at the representation level: the 4D encoding captures multi-way clinical relationships that improved classification and supported severity prediction in this proof-of-concept study. Transfer to an independent hospital was most robust for exacerbation risk, whereas fine-grained three-way classification remained affected by cross-source distribution shift and infection-label boundary noise. Multicenter, multidisease validation is the necessary next step.

title: Title: Probabilistic Logic Programming with Dynamic Contextualization
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic logic programming framework designed to enhance reasoning capabilities in systems dealing with uncertainty and dynamic environments. Standard logic programming techniques often struggle with incomplete information, requiring significant manual intervention. We introduce a dynamic contextualization mechanism that updates the program's internal state based on observed data, incorporating a model of the surrounding context. This allows the system to reason more effectively about uncertainty and adapt to changing conditions, addressing limitations of current approaches and offering a promising path towards more robust and flexible logical reasoning. The core of our design is a probabilistic system that iteratively refines the program's internal representation, incorporating observed data and a dynamically updated model of the context. We explore a specific implementation utilizing a Bayesian updating approach to model the contextual shift, demonstrating its potential for improved performance in complex scenarios.

title: Title: Adaptive Neural Network Activation Function Design
abstract: This paper explores the design of an adaptive neural network activation function that dynamically adjusts its parameters based on the inherent non-linearity of input data. The core challenge in traditional neural networks is their inability to effectively model complex, non-linear relationships within the data, limiting their expressive power. This work proposes a novel activation function architecture that incorporates a self-adjusting parameter system, allowing the network to adapt to the specific characteristics of the input and improve model performance. We introduce a mechanism for dynamically modifying the activation function's parameters, thereby enabling the network to better represent and learn from the data's underlying structure. The resulting activation function demonstrates improved accuracy and robustness in a range of neural network tasks, particularly when dealing with data exhibiting significant non-linearity. The proposed approach offers a significant advancement in neural network design, addressing a critical limitation in many applications.

title: Dynamic Neuron Connection Weight-Dependent Adaptive Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of dynamic neuron connection weights in adaptive learning systems. The central claim is that neuron connection weights are not static but rather adapt dynamically based on internal neuron states and environmental changes. This dynamic adjustment is proposed as a core mechanism to improve learning efficiency. The research challenges the traditional assumption of static connection weights in neural networks by exploring the impact of dynamic weights on learning performance. A model is designed incorporating feedback mechanisms and adaptive algorithms to facilitate this dynamic weight adjustment. The investigation aims to provide a theoretical framework and demonstrate the advantages of a dynamic approach to learning compared to conventional static weight models. The key mathematical formulation explores the relationship between neuron state, environmental input, and the updated connection weights. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of neural network learning and suggests a novel pathway for designing more efficient and robust adaptive learning systems.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Optimization via Game Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the application of game theory optimization techniques to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) environments. The core claim centers around leveraging the optimization methodologies inherent in game theory to enhance the collaborative efficiency and overall performance of multi-agent systems. The primary mechanism involves constructing a MARL environment and employing game-theoretic mechanism design principles to refine agent strategies and communication protocols. Specifically, we explore how techniques from cooperative game theory, such as Nash equilibrium analysis and Shapley value calculations, can be integrated into the learning process within a multi-agent setting. This approach directly addresses the inherent challenges of MARL, particularly the issues of strategy conflict and resource competition among agents. The research demonstrates a potential pathway for improved coordination and decision-making in complex multi-agent scenarios. The theoretical framework presented provides a novel approach to MARL optimization, offering a structured methodology for designing and implementing efficient multi-agent systems.

title: Adaptive Data Augmentation for Deep Learning in Low-Data Regimes
abstract: Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success across various domains, largely due to the availability of large datasets. However, obtaining such extensive datasets is often a significant challenge, particularly in specialized fields or scenarios where data acquisition is expensive or time-consuming. In these low-data regimes, traditional data augmentation techniques frequently prove ineffective, often exacerbating model overfitting rather than improving generalization. This paper introduces an adaptive data augmentation strategy designed to address this limitation. The core idea is to create a feedback loop wherein the augmentation process dynamically adjusts based on the model's current state, prioritizing regions of high uncertainty. We formulate this approach using a Bayesian neural network framework, allowing for the quantification and targeted amplification of data in areas where the model's predictive confidence is weakest. The proposed method demonstrates improved performance compared to static augmentation techniques in low-data settings, showcasing the potential of adaptive augmentation for boosting deep learning model robustness and accuracy when data is scarce.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Adaptive Rule Generation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to artificial intelligence—Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Adaptive Rule Generation—designed to overcome limitations inherent in traditional rule-based systems and deep learning models. The core idea is to combine the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with the representational and reasoning power of symbolic programming. This synergy allows for the dynamic generation and refinement of symbolic rules directly from raw data, leading to more adaptable, explainable, and efficient intelligent systems. The system operates through a closed-loop mechanism: a neural network identifies salient patterns within data, and a symbolic engine then constructs and iteratively improves rules based on these patterns. This adaptive process addresses the challenge of brittle rule sets in traditional systems and the lack of interpretability in deep learning. The paper outlines the architecture of the system, details the adaptive rule generation process, and discusses the potential applications and future research directions.

title: Graph-Based Anomaly Detection with Relational Reasoning
abstract: Anomaly detection in graph data presents unique challenges due to the inherent complexity of relationships between nodes. Existing methods often rely on isolated node features or simple graph metrics, failing to adequately capture the intricate dependencies that define anomalous behavior. This paper proposes a novel approach to graph anomaly detection that leverages graph embedding techniques coupled with relational reasoning algorithms. The core idea is to learn rich representations of graph structures and their relationships, and then identify deviations from expected patterns using rule-based systems or other relational reasoning methods. We demonstrate that this approach significantly improves anomaly detection accuracy compared to traditional methods by explicitly modeling and analyzing the relational context of graph nodes and edges. The system is designed to detect anomalies by identifying nodes or edges that exhibit unusual relational patterns. The proposed methodology offers a more nuanced and effective strategy for detecting graph anomalies, particularly in scenarios where relationships are crucial to understanding normal and abnormal behavior.

title: 基于量子自旋的动态拓扑算法的自适应参数调整
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic topology algorithm based on quantum spin dynamics. Traditional optimization algorithms often rely on static parameter settings, limiting their effectiveness. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the quantum spin parameters, allowing for more efficient parameter tuning and improved algorithm performance. The algorithm leverages the inherent properties of quantum spin to iteratively refine the system's state, leading to enhanced results. The core mechanism involves a self-consistent update loop that modifies the spin states based on a predefined objective function. This approach offers a fundamentally different perspective on parameter optimization, potentially yielding superior outcomes compared to conventional methods. We detail the algorithm's design, theoretical analysis, and preliminary experimental validation, demonstrating its effectiveness in a specific quantum optimization problem.

title: Neuromorphic Computing for Procedural Content Generation
abstract: Procedural content generation (PCG) has become a cornerstone of modern game development and creative design, offering automated methods for producing vast and diverse content. However, conventional PCG algorithms often rely on computationally intensive techniques like Monte Carlo simulations or complex rule-based systems, leading to performance bottlenecks and limitations in generating truly novel and complex structures. This paper proposes a novel approach to PCG utilizing neuromorphic computing, specifically employing Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs). SNNs, inspired by the biological brain, offer inherent parallel processing capabilities and energy efficiency, making them ideally suited for real-time content generation. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of mapping PCG algorithms onto SNNs, focusing on the translation of iterative processes into spiking events. The core claim is that leveraging the inherent parallelism of SNNs allows for the creation of significantly more complex and varied content compared to traditional methods. We present a framework for designing SNNs for specific PCG tasks, including level generation, landscape modeling, and architectural design. The potential for achieving unprecedented levels of realism and complexity in content generation is highlighted, demonstrating a shift in paradigm for creative algorithms. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and future directions of this emerging field, including the optimization of SNN architectures and the development of novel PCG algorithms specifically tailored for neuromorphic hardware.

title: Ads from automatons: Consumer perceptions of AI modality disclosures and the roles of AI experience and dispositional persuasion knowledge on advertising outcomes
abstract: Extant literature on consumer reactions to AI-generated advertising have focused on resulting perceptions of creativity, objectivity, and effectiveness in specific situations, often invoking situational persuasion knowledge as a framework to guide explanations of reactions. Though informative, this leaves a research gap with regard to other forms of persuasion knowledge, ad contexts, and advertising-relevant outcomes. Through an experimental approach and in response to platform-specific guidelines and proposed laws mandating disclosures of AI-generated content in advertising, the current study seeks to understand the interaction of dispositional persuasion knowledge, experience with AI tools, and trust in AI to better explain consumer reactions to online banner ad elements labeled as generated by AI. We find a general consumer ambivalence toward advertising disclosed as AI-generated vs. a non-AI-generated control (regardless of AI-generated modality), but also novel positive effects of dispositional persuasion knowledge, AI experience, and trust in AI with regard to specific advertising-focused dependent variables when the use of AI-generated text in ads is disclosed. Theoretical and practical takeaways for marketers are discussed.

title: Interpretable Temporal Video Reasoning with EventGraph and EventField
abstract: We present a structured temporal video reasoning pipeline built around a discrete EventGraph, a continuous EventField, and a human-readable EventGlyph view. On a calibrated EPIC-KITCHENS subset of 10 videos and 50 temporal reasoning questions, EventField+Glyph achieves 0.98 overall accuracy, which is higher than the caption baseline by +0.40 (paired p = 1.1 \times 10^{-5}) and direct VLM-only QA by +0.20 (p = 0.0063) on this subset. We further evaluate annotation-source variations, including manual, heuristic, and heuristic+Gemini pipelines, and find that the best structured method stays above the caption baseline across settings. We also include cross-video pair benchmarking and an appendix gallery of glyph outputs for all studied videos. Overall, the results indicate that structured temporal representations can support both performance and inspectability by preserving symbolic structure, capturing temporal continuity, and providing human-readable diagnostics for video reasoning.

title: Uni-Light: An Ultra-Lightweight Framework via Uncertainty-Aware Knowledge Distillation for Brain Tumour Segmentation
abstract: Accurate 3D brain tumour segmentation from multi-modal Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is essential for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning. Existing brain tumour segmentation methods often suffer from heavy computational demands, while current lightweight architectures frequently lack the capacity to maintain segmentation fidelity in complex tumour regions. To address these issues, we propose a novel ultra-lightweight framework (Uni-Light) that achieves high-fidelity segmentation with substantially reduced computational overhead. It combines multi-scale convolutions with an uncertainty-aware knowledge distillation scheme that directs the student model toward hard-to-classify regions, complemented by a Signed Distance Field boundary loss for geometric constraints. Experimental results on BraTS2023-GLI and MSD-BTS datasets demonstrate that Uni-Light reduces parameters by 97.56%, floating-point operations (FLOPs) by 73.03%, and inference memory footprint by 81.58%, while surpassing the state-of-the-art model by an average of 1.47% in Dice score, offering a highly competitive trade-off between segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency in resource-constrained clinical settings. This work also advances data engineering for medical imaging by demonstrating that teacher model uncertainty can be exploited as a data-driven supervisory signal, re-prioritising the training data distribution without requiring additional annotation.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Geometric Topology Modeling
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental quantum phenomenon, offers a potential pathway to revolutionize geometric topology modeling. This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement to construct a robust and complex geometric topology model. The core claim is that leveraging entanglement allows for the exploration of topological properties and the creation of a model that surpasses classical approaches in geometric understanding. We detail the core mechanism, outlining how entanglement facilitates the generation of intricate geometric structures and the analysis of their stability. The paper presents a foundational framework for utilizing entanglement to create a more precise geometric model.

title: Quantum Topology Field Theory Simulation Framework for Adaptive Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum Topology Field Theory (QTTF) offers a novel approach to quantum computation by leveraging the topological properties of spacetime. This paper proposes a self-adaptive quantum computing simulation framework, designed to efficiently model complex systems and dynamically adjust quantum parameters based on simulation results. We introduce a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism based on the inherent properties of QTTF, enabling precise simulation of quantum behavior and enhancing accuracy compared to traditional static simulation methods. The framework's core principle lies in constructing a quantum computational model that evolves in response to the simulation process, fostering a self-correcting and adaptable simulation methodology. The key contribution of this work is the development of a robust and flexible simulation framework that can effectively handle the intricacies of quantum systems, offering a significant advancement in the field of adaptive quantum computing.

title: Algorithmic Self-Repair in Adaptive Neural Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for achieving algorithmic self-repair in adaptive neural networks. Traditional adaptive neural networks often struggle with catastrophic forgetting – the tendency to lose previously learned knowledge when trained on new data. This paper introduces a dynamic weight adjustment mechanism, termed the "Error-Correction Loop," that proactively analyzes network output and automatically adjusts weights to mitigate errors and enhance performance. The core mechanism centers around a real-time error analysis and iterative weight refinement, addressing a significant challenge in continual learning and boosting the robustness of these networks. We detail the algorithm's design, performance evaluation, and potential implications for machine learning systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Phase Field Control
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a unique opportunity to manipulate the fundamental fabric of reality. This paper explores the potential of leveraging entanglement to control phase shifts within a vacuum, proposing a novel technique centered around dynamically entangled 'entanglement fields' for precise spacetime modulation. We detail the core mechanism of maintaining entanglement with a complex multi-dimensional space, outlining a design that could revolutionize the manipulation of phase and potentially, spacetime itself. The proposed method offers a fundamentally new approach to quantum field manipulation, moving beyond passive observation and towards active, controlled phase shifts. This research investigates the theoretical and potential practical implications of this concept, acknowledging the challenges and outlining future research directions.

This research investigates the theoretical and potential practical implications of this concept, acknowledging the challenges and outlining future research directions.

title: Title: Adaptive Topology of Quantum Measurement Spaces (ATQM)
abstract: Quantum measurement protocols are inherently complex, requiring careful consideration of the measurement space to maximize information gained. Traditional approaches often assume a fixed measurement space, limiting the potential for optimization. This paper introduces Adaptive Topology of Quantum Measurement Spaces (ATQM), a novel protocol that dynamically reshapes the quantum state based on machine learning, leading to significant improvements in information extraction from quantum measurements. This adaptive approach offers a more intelligent and flexible framework for measurement design, addressing limitations of existing protocols and opening new avenues for quantum computation.

title: Topological Phase Field for Quantum Algorithm Optimization
abstract: Quantum algorithm optimization presents a significant challenge in the field of quantum computing. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the inherent complexities of quantum systems, leading to unpredictable and suboptimal solutions. This paper proposes a novel Topological Phase Field (TPF) – a mathematical framework designed to guide the evolution of quantum states during optimization. We introduce a new model that dynamically adjusts the quantum state based on a predefined evolution pattern, mitigating the issues associated with conventional optimization techniques. This framework aims to achieve significantly improved convergence rates and robustness in quantum algorithm execution. This work offers a fundamentally new approach to optimizing quantum algorithms by leveraging the principles of topological phase fields, demonstrating potential improvements in both performance and stability.

title: Quantum Bio Reaction Simulation
abstract: Quantum Bio Reaction Simulation (QBRS) is a novel quantum simulation framework designed to model complex biological reactions with unprecedented accuracy. The core innovation lies in leveraging quantum entanglement to create a self-organizing quantum system capable of mimicking intricate biological processes. This simulation aims to provide a significantly more precise approach to drug design, biological effect prediction, and fundamental biological research than traditional computational methods. The algorithm's unique mechanism exploits quantum correlations to enhance the fidelity of simulations, offering a shift from classical approximations to a fundamentally deeper understanding of biological systems. This paper details the architecture, implementation, and preliminary results of QBRS, highlighting its potential to revolutionize biological modeling and drug discovery.

title: Title: Modular Quantum State Collapse (MQSC)
abstract: Quantum state collapse is a fundamental process in quantum mechanics, representing the irreversible transition from a superposition of states to a single, definite state. Traditional approaches to quantum computation often involve a single, global collapse, which presents significant challenges in terms of scalability and error correction. This paper introduces Modular Quantum State Collapse (MQSC), a novel framework for efficiently collapsing multiple quantum states simultaneously. MQSC leverages a set of modular operations designed to selectively collapse multiple parts of a system, dramatically reducing the computational burden inherent in conventional approaches. We propose a new methodology for managing and manipulating quantum states, offering a fundamentally different perspective on quantum computation. This paper details the design of these modular operations, explores their impact on computational complexity, and discusses potential applications of MQSC in various quantum computing paradigms. The core claim of this research is that MQSC provides a significantly more efficient and scalable approach to quantum state manipulation, paving the way for advancements in quantum information processing.

title: High-Dimensional Data Distribution Clustering with Adaptive Adjustment
abstract: High-dimensional data distribution clustering is a challenging problem due to the inherent complexity of the data. Traditional methods often struggle to effectively handle high-dimensional data, leading to suboptimal clustering results. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, termed "Adaptive High-Dimensional Data Distribution Clustering," designed to address this challenge by incorporating an adaptive learning mechanism. The algorithm dynamically adjusts cluster parameters based on the input data, enabling it to automatically optimize the clustering process and discover more effective groupings. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously evaluates the clustering quality and adjusts the parameters accordingly. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and experimental results, showcasing its ability to outperform existing methods in terms of cluster quality and efficiency.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Coding and Decoding Framework (QICF)
abstract: This paper presents the Quantum Entanglement Information Coding and Decoding Framework (QICF), a novel approach to quantum information processing designed to overcome the limitations of classical communication channels and mitigate information loss. The core claim of QICF is the utilization of multi-body quantum entanglement to achieve information encoding and decoding rates surpassing those attainable through classical channels. The framework is predicated on a mechanism involving precisely controlled generation and measurement of entanglement within a superconducting qubit array. We leverage the quantum coherence inherent in entangled states for efficient information encoding and decoding, complemented by a robust error correction protocol. Unlike traditional single-qubit-based quantum coding schemes, QICF's utilization of multi-body entanglement offers significant advantages in terms of encoding efficiency and error resilience. This work details the theoretical underpinnings of QICF, outlining the key components and operational principles. We propose a framework for implementing QICF using current superconducting qubit technology, acknowledging the challenges and potential improvements. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate the feasibility of achieving reliable quantum communication and information processing through the exploitation of entangled quantum states.

title: Probabilistic Graphical Models Based on Spatial Data Structures
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to enhancing the efficiency of probabilistic graphical model inference by leveraging spatial data structures. Traditional probabilistic graphical models (PGMs) often struggle with scalability when dealing with large spatial datasets, leading to computationally expensive inference processes. This research proposes a framework that integrates PGMs with spatial indexing structures, such as k-d trees and R-trees, to significantly accelerate inference speed. The core idea is to utilize the spatial locality inherent in the data to reduce the search space for nodes during probabilistic reasoning. The proposed method offers a practical solution for modeling and reasoning about spatial data, opening up opportunities for applications in areas like environmental modeling, urban planning, and anomaly detection. This paper details the theoretical foundations, the proposed integration mechanism, and discusses the potential performance gains compared to traditional approaches.

title: Quantum Entangled Matrices: An Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a fundamentally different approach to matrix computation, potentially surpassing classical methods in certain scenarios. This paper proposes a novel optimization algorithm specifically tailored for quantum entanglement, aiming to enhance the efficiency of matrix operations. We introduce a quantum state manipulation scheme leveraging entanglement to achieve a significant speedup in calculations, addressing limitations inherent in current quantum computing architectures. The core mechanism centers around strategically manipulating entangled qubit states to represent and manipulate matrix elements, offering a pathway to dramatically accelerate matrix computations. The algorithm's novelty lies in its incorporation of quantum entanglement as a key computational resource, providing a unique advantage over existing optimization strategies. We detail the algorithm's architecture, the quantum circuit implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating improved performance compared to classical methods. This work explores the potential of entanglement to fundamentally alter matrix computation, presenting a promising avenue for advancing quantum computing capabilities.

title: Temporal Anomaly Detection via Phase-Space Reconstruction
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to temporal anomaly detection by leveraging the principles of phase-space reconstruction. The core idea centers on mapping a time series data into a high-dimensional phase space, reconstructing this space using manifold learning techniques, and then identifying anomalies as deviations from the expected manifold structure. This method offers a robust and potentially effective solution for anomaly detection in various time-series applications. The paper details the methodology, outlining the key steps involved in the reconstruction process and the criteria used for anomaly identification. We demonstrate the applicability of this approach through a theoretical framework, highlighting its potential advantages over traditional anomaly detection methods. The primary focus is on the mathematical underpinnings and the conceptual framework, providing a foundational understanding for future research and implementation. The proposed technique aims to provide a systematic approach to analyzing temporal data and uncovering hidden patterns indicative of anomalous behavior.

title: Algorithmic Bias Detection in Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources, preserving data privacy. However, the inherent data heterogeneity across clients introduces a significant challenge: algorithmic bias. This paper presents a novel method for detecting and quantifying bias within the federated learning process. Our approach leverages statistical measures and differential privacy techniques to monitor model updates and identify bias amplification. We define key metrics such as variance of model updates, divergence between client models, and the sensitivity of model predictions to sensitive attributes. The core of our method is the adaptive adjustment of learning rates based on these metrics, aiming to mitigate bias while maintaining model convergence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, highlighting its potential for robust and fair FL systems. The proposed framework provides a quantifiable assessment of bias risk and suggests strategies for bias mitigation during the training process.

title: CogSent: Cognition-Driven Multimodal Sentiment Analysis Through Fast–Slow Thinking
abstract: Sentiment analysis of multimodal social media data is of great importance, not only for recognizing objective information but also for capturing subjective emotional states. While single-modal sentiment analysis has achieved notable progress, existing multimodal approaches still face two key challenges: (1) inadequate modeling of subjective emotional characteristics and (2) insufficient handling of cross-modal inconsistencies. To address these limitations, we propose an image-text multimodal sentiment analysis framework (CogSent) grounded in the psychological Dual-System Theory. First, inspired by human fast and slow thinking, we develop a Hierarchical Dual-Channel Cognition (HDCC) architecture to extract intuitive and rational affective features, respectively. Second, we introduce an Intuition-Guided Cognition Refinement (IGCR) module that uses System-I-inspired intuitive representations as affective priors to retrieve and refine System-II-inspired contextual representations via cross-attention. Third, we propose a Dynamic Cross-Modal Cognition Fusion (DC2F) network that predicts sample-adaptive thresholds from modality discrepancy, agreement, and attention statistics, dynamically regulating directional image–text interaction to mitigate interference from conflicting cross-modal sentiment signals. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate that CogSent achieves improved performance compared to existing methods and yields competitive results on multiple evaluation settings.

title: Back to the Feature: Zero-Shot 6DoF Pose Estimation via Dense Local Features
abstract: We present B2TFPose, a training-free zero-shot method for 6DoF pose estimation of unseen objects from RGB images. Using a single frozen DINOv3 vision transformer as its only pretrained component within the pose estimation pipeline, B2TFPose extracts dense patch-level features that generalize across the synthetic-to-real domain gap without any task-specific fine-tuning, revisiting the classical local feature matching paradigm through the lens of large-scale self-supervised foundation models. Three contributions advance the training-free state of the art. A geodesic non-maximum suppression strategy retrieves a viewpoint-diverse template set for coarse-to-fine correspondence matching. Render-guided Re-Correspondence (RRC) synthesizes object-specific views at the estimated pose and re-establishes dense 2D-3D correspondences to sharpen the initial estimate without additional learned parameters. A multi-mask hypothesis selection strategy jointly scores competing segmentation candidates to resolve segmentation ambiguity. On the seven core datasets of the BOP Benchmark, B2TFPose achieves 40.7 mean AR without refinement and 56.4 with refinement, establishing state-of-the-art performance among training-free RGB methods and outperforming trained counterparts including GigaPose and GenFlow, at competitive inference speed.

title: InsightChain: Optimized Chain-of-Insight Analytics for LLM-driven Data Visualization
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for automated data visualization, yet existing approaches often frame visualization generation as a single-step mapping from user query to figure or code, overlooking the iterative analytical reasoning process of expert analysts. We present InsightChain, a four-stage visualization prompting pipeline (Explore--Focus--Test--Present) that emulates expert analytical workflows, together with VG-COPRO, a vision-guided automatic prompt optimization (APO) method adapted to jointly optimize such multi-stage, executable pipelines. To address the evaluation gap for complex data visualization, we introduce the Insight Progression Metric (IPM), a rubric combining four text-based dimensions with a vision-based dimension. We assess IPM through a 100-chain human pilot and an expanded 300-chain agent-based evaluation spanning all ten domains. Experiments on public datasets show that InsightChain consistently outperforms competing prompting baselines. Existing APO methods fail to yield consistent gains on this multi-stage task, whereas VG-COPRO improves performance in both in-domain and cross-domain settings.

title: El ocaso del espejismo de la IA Agéntica: análisis crítico de costos ocultos, vulnerabilidades de inyección de prompts e inmunidad de infraestructura en sistemas corporativos. Un enfoque desde la experiencia de la Ingeniería de Datos y la seguridad de redes
abstract: El presente artículo analiza la viabilidad económica, operativa y de seguridad de la integración de agentes de Inteligencia Artificial (IA) autónomos en sistemas de Planificación de Recursos Empresariales (ERP) y Gestión de Relaciones con Clientes (CRM). Frente a la narrativa comercial que postula el reemplazo total del modelo de Software como Servicio (SaaS), este documento expone la fragilidad estructural del enfoque agéntico basado en APIs de terceros debido al denominado “impuesto del token” y a los bucles recurrentes de retroalimentación (prompt looping). Adicionalmente, se desmitifica la simplicidad de la implementación de Modelos de Lenguaje Pequeños (SLMs) en entornos locales, detallando la deuda técnica y las restricciones asociadas a la cuantización y la orquestación. Desde la perspectiva de la ciberseguridad, se evalúa el riesgo sistémico de la adopción de plataformas como OpenClaw dentro de clústeres corporativos, considerando la viabilidad de ataques por inyección malintencionada de prompts, escapes de contenedor y movimientos laterales en redes puente. Finalmente, se propone un modelo de inmunidad digital fundamentado en una arquitectura asíncrona estrictamente desvinculada de la red (airgapped) y una política de Confianza Cero basada en validación humana mediante comandos de privilegios altos controlados asociados a claves temporales encriptadas generadas desde autenticadores criptográficos físicos.

title: Title: Self-Organizing Morphological Networks – Pattern Recognition Through Emergent Structure
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-organizing network architecture designed for pattern recognition, specifically focusing on the automatic construction and evolution of morphological patterns within data. Recognizing the limitations of traditional machine learning approaches, which often require extensive manual feature engineering, we introduce the "Dynamic Morphological Re-ordering" algorithm as the core mechanism for generating complex and adaptable patterns. This algorithm iteratively refines the network's structure based on local feedback, fostering emergent behavior and allowing for the discovery of intricate patterns without explicit design. We detail the algorithm's design, its underlying principles, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying and classifying diverse patterns. The paper explores the potential applications of this architecture across various pattern recognition tasks, highlighting its ability to automatically generate robust and adaptable morphological representations.

abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol, termed "Adaptive Quantum Key Distribution Protocol Optimization Algorithm," designed to enhance both security and efficiency through dynamic optimization of quantum entanglement control. title: Algorithmic Quantum Simulation of Biological Systems
abstract: This paper explores the potential of algorithmic quantum simulation to revolutionize the study of biological systems. Biological systems exhibit intricate, non-linear interactions that are exceedingly challenging for classical computational methods. Quantum computers, with their unique ability to represent and manipulate quantum states, offer a paradigm shift in this domain. title: Quantum-Inspired Cryptography with Entangled State Analysis
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum-inspired cryptography leveraging the complexities of entangled quantum states. Current quantum-inspired schemes often utilize simplified models, which lack the inherent security guarantees provided by genuine quantum phenomena. This research proposes a cryptographic protocol fundamentally rooted in the analysis and manipulation of entanglement. The core mechanism involves developing sophisticated techniques for measuring and controlling entangled states to generate key exchange and encryption/decryption processes. We demonstrate that this approach, utilizing the full potential of quantum mechanics, results in a significantly more robust and secure system compared to existing quantum-inspired methods. The protocol incorporates novel methods for key distribution based on the probabilistic nature of entanglement measurements and employs a multi-level security approach to mitigate potential vulnerabilities. The analysis presented focuses on the mathematical underpinnings of the protocol, detailing the operations performed on entangled states and the resultant security properties. We provide a comprehensive theoretical framework for evaluating the security of the proposed system, exploring potential attacks and demonstrating the protocol's resilience. The key contributions of this work include the formalization of the entanglement-based key exchange process and the development of a security model specifically tailored to the unique characteristics of entangled quantum states.

title: Spectral Graph Embedding with Learnable Fourier Transforms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to spectral graph embedding that addresses the limitations of existing methods in capturing high-frequency patterns within graph data. The core idea is to integrate learnable Fourier transforms directly into the embedding process. This allows the algorithm to explicitly model and extract complex, high-frequency features from the graph Laplacian spectrum. We demonstrate that this technique significantly improves the ability to represent graph structure, leading to more effective embeddings for downstream tasks such as node classification and graph clustering. The primary contribution is the development of a framework that dynamically adapts to the specific spectral characteristics of a graph, offering a more nuanced and powerful approach compared to static spectral embedding techniques. The proposed method leverages the inherent periodicity and oscillations present in graph Laplacian spectra, which are often missed by traditional methods. The learned Fourier transforms are trained alongside the embedding vectors, optimizing both for graph representation and spectral feature extraction. This approach offers a significant improvement in capturing intricate graph structures, particularly those with high-frequency components.

title: Based on Time Compression Quantum Information Transmission Protocol
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum information transmission protocol leveraging time compression techniques to enhance transmission rates. The core principle involves compressing the temporal dimensions of quantum signals, thereby reducing the overall time required for information transfer. We introduce a framework for implementing this protocol, outlining the key steps and considerations for successful execution. The protocol utilizes Bell states and employs a time-encoding scheme to represent quantum information. The time compression process is achieved through a series of measurements and reconstructions, effectively reducing the duration of the transmitted signal without altering the underlying quantum information. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the potential for significant rate improvements compared to conventional quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols. This work offers a new perspective on quantum information transmission, combining the strengths of time compression with the inherent security features of quantum mechanics. We present a detailed mathematical description of the protocol, focusing on the key equations governing the time compression and reconstruction stages. This protocol represents a significant step towards achieving higher-speed quantum communication. ---

title: Algorithmic Cryptography – Dynamic Key Generation via Quantum-Enhanced Random Number Generation
abstract: This paper introduces an algorithmic cryptographic system predicated on dynamic key generation utilizing quantum-enhanced random number generation. Traditional cryptographic methods rely on deterministic processes and computational complexity, making them susceptible to various attacks. We propose a novel approach that leverages quantum superposition and entanglement to produce keys with substantially higher entropy and resistance to known attacks. The core mechanism centers around establishing a 'seed' – a fundamentally unpredictable state – within a quantum system that serves as the foundation for generating truly random keys. The system's design incorporates advanced quantum algorithms to enhance the randomness and security of key creation. This research explores the potential of quantum-enhanced randomness to revolutionize key generation, offering a significant advancement over existing methods.

abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement to achieve ultra-high bandwidth communication, addressing the limitations imposed by classical communication channels. The core concept revolves around leveraging the instantaneous correlation inherent in entangled particles to establish secure and high-capacity communication links. We delve into the theoretical framework, focusing on quantum key distribution (QKD) and broader quantum communication protocols enhanced by entanglement. The paper details how manipulating entangled states could lead to information transfer rates exceeding those achievable through conventional methods. While a full experimental demonstration remains a significant challenge, this work lays out a foundation for future research and technological advancements in this burgeoning field. We present a novel approach to bandwidth scaling by fundamentally altering the information transmission paradigm. The proposed architecture utilizes multi-particle entanglement to encode and transmit data, offering a theoretical pathway to drastically increased communication speeds. This research contributes to the ongoing exploration of quantum communication and its transformative potential. ---

title: Quantum Key Distribution Protocol Based on Quantum Coherence Dephasing
abstract: This paper presents a novel Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocol leveraging the phenomenon of quantum coherence dephasing to enhance security. The protocol, termed Coherence Dephasing Key Distribution (CDKD), utilizes the inherent fragility of quantum states to create a robust key exchange mechanism. The core principle involves encoding key information within a quantum state subject to dephasing, effectively mitigating the impact of eavesdropping attempts. Mathematical analysis demonstrates the protocol's resilience against various attack scenarios, particularly those exploiting known vulnerabilities in traditional QKD protocols. The proposed protocol offers a promising approach to secure key distribution, particularly in environments where sophisticated eavesdropping techniques are anticipated. The security relies on the fundamental uncertainty principle and the sensitivity of quantum states to environmental noise, specifically focusing on the dephasing process. The key equation governing the protocol is: $E = ħω \cos(\Delta \phi)$, where $E$ is the energy, $ħ$ is the reduced Planck constant, $\omega$ is the angular frequency, and $\Delta \phi$ is the phase difference. The protocol's security is fundamentally tied to maintaining a significant phase uncertainty, which is achieved through careful control of the quantum state and the introduction of appropriate dephasing mechanisms. This work provides a theoretical framework for the CDKD protocol and highlights its potential for practical implementation.

title: Distributed Learning with Personalized Experience Replay for Federated IoT
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources, such as Internet of Things (IoT) devices, without directly exchanging raw data. However, the practical deployment of FL in IoT environments is hindered by several key challenges, including significant data heterogeneity across devices and the limited computational and storage resources inherent in these devices. This paper proposes a novel distributed learning framework that addresses these limitations by incorporating personalized experience replay (PER). PER allows each IoT device to store a representative subset of its training data and periodically replay past experiences to refine its local model. This mechanism not only mitigates the effects of data heterogeneity but also improves model convergence and accuracy, particularly in scenarios where individual devices have sparse or biased data. The proposed approach maintains user privacy by operating locally on device data, and the distributed nature of the framework reduces the communication overhead typically associated with FL. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components and design considerations for a practical implementation. The core claim is that federated learning in IoT devices faces challenges with data heterogeneity and limited computational resources. The core mechanism is to implement a distributed learning framework incorporating personalized experience replay, where each IoT device stores a subset of its training data and periodically replays experiences to improve model performance, while preserving user privacy. This approach represents a significant advancement in FL for IoT, enabling more robust and accurate models in resource-constrained environments.

title: ADELE - Adaptive Delaunay Grids for High-Fidelity Mesh-Native Reconstruction
abstract: Meshes remain the most practical representation for geometry reasoning and integration into graphics pipelines, yet existing reconstruction methods struggle to produce high-quality meshes. Most state-of-the-art approaches initially learn an intermediate representation (NeRF/3DGS) and treat mesh extraction as a post-processing step, which often leads to oversmoothed surfaces or poor quality meshes with excessive triangle counts.Existing mesh-native optimization methods alleviate some of these issues but suffer from fixed-resolution discretizations and unstable optimization behavior. In this paper, we introduce an adaptive mesh-based optimization framework and a practical mesh rendering technique to address these challenges. Our representation combines an optimizable Delaunay-triangulated tetrahedral grid with a multi-resolution hash grid. The former is refined through point pruning and insertion, while the latter provides latent features for SDF/appearance value predictions. We use volumetric rendering to bootstrap a coarse geometry while leveraging mesh-based rendering for recovering fine-grained details. Additionally, we propose a differentiable, rasterization-based depth-offset rendering formulation, reducing geometric artifacts and improving reconstruction quality. Our method significantly outperforms existing mesh optimization approaches across a variety of object-centric benchmarks while being competitive with state-of-the-art NeRF/3DGS methods.

title: Large-Scale Pretraining for Improving Deep Learning-Based Geometric Distortion Correction of Diffusion-Weighted Imaging
abstract: Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) is widely used in clinical settings but remains vulnerable to geometric distortion. Conventional correction methods often require additional acquisitions or vendor-specific solutions, limiting their feasibility in high-throughput, resource-constrained settings. This study investigates whether large-scale pretraining strategies can improve deep learning-based distortion correction for single-phase-encoding DWI. We formulate the task as image reconstruction, and compare a non-pretrained baseline against a self-supervised and a generative pretrained model, evaluated using both quantitative image-similarity metrics and qualitative expert assessment. The best-performing model was further tested for transferability on data collected in an LMIC setting with acquisition shift. Pretrained models outperformed the non-pretrained baseline, with cWDM achieving the strongest results across both quantitative and qualitative evaluation. However, application to LMIC data revealed transferability challenges, including contrast alteration and over-reliance on T1-weighted anatomical structure. Registering images to a common standard space improved predictions, suggesting that harmonized preprocessing may enhance cross-domain deployment.

abstract: This paper introduces Hyper-Adaptive Modular Logic (HAL), a novel logic system designed to overcome the limitations of traditional modular logic by dynamically adjusting its structure and axioms in response to the specific context of a calculation. abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is a promising technology for secure communication, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to ensure the confidentiality of transmitted data. This paper explores the application of a probabilistic quantum key distribution (QKD) algorithm, employing a novel approach based on quantum entanglement and topology to provide a rigorous security proof. The core mechanism involves exploiting the inherent probabilistic nature of quantum systems to demonstrate the algorithm's resistance to eavesdropping. We provide a detailed mathematical framework and justification for the proposed proof, emphasizing the role of topology in shaping the security properties. This research aims to advance the understanding of QKD's security through a probabilistic framework, offering a distinct approach to guarantee secure key exchange.

title: Bayesian Geometric Chaos with Adaptive Parameter Tuning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian framework for modeling chaotic systems, incorporating adaptive parameter tuning to enhance predictive accuracy. The core mechanism leverages a learned 'chaos curve' as a surrogate to drastically reduce computational costs associated with Bayesian inference. The algorithm dynamically adjusts parameters based on observed data, creating a continuous feedback loop that improves the model's ability to capture system dynamics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive analysis on diverse systems, showcasing significant improvements in predictive performance compared to existing methods. The paper highlights the benefits of this framework for complex, high-dimensional scenarios.

title: Title: Adaptive Topology for Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive topology to algorithm design, aiming to optimize efficiency by dynamically adjusting algorithm structure based on runtime evaluation. The core mechanism centers around an iterative evaluation and structural refinement process. The challenge of finding optimal algorithm structures is highlighted as a significant hurdle in algorithm design, and this work proposes a novel approach leveraging continuous structural assessment and adjustment. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, evaluation metrics, and preliminary results demonstrating the potential for improved performance through this adaptive system. We will present a comprehensive illustration of the system's operation, focusing on its ability to respond to runtime changes and enhance algorithm effectiveness. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential implications for algorithm design.

title: Title: Self-Organizing Constraint Networks for Adaptive Machine Learning
abstract: This paper explores the application of Self-Organizing Constraint Networks (SOCN) to adaptive machine learning. Traditional machine learning often relies on predefined constraints, limiting the model's flexibility and potential for robust performance. We propose a novel architecture, SOCN, that dynamically generates and optimizes constraint networks to adapt to the specific demands of each machine learning task. The core mechanism involves a reinforcement learning loop, allowing the network to iteratively refine its structure and constraints based on the learning process itself. This approach mimics the biological neural network design principles, potentially leading to more adaptable and robust models compared to current state-of-the-art techniques. We present a preliminary implementation and demonstrate the efficacy of SOCN in a simulated task, showcasing its ability to achieve improved performance with minimal manual tuning. This work contributes to a shift towards autonomous constraint optimization, paving the way for more adaptable and efficient machine learning systems.

title: Quantum Topology in Nonlinear Topology Adaptive Algorithms
abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly evolving field, offers a fundamentally new approach to computational design and optimization. This paper explores the potential of quantum topology in developing adaptive algorithms for complex systems, specifically focusing on the design and implementation of a novel non-linear topology adaptive algorithm. We present a core claim outlining the fundamental concept of a "Quantum Topology Adaptive Algorithm" (QTAA) – an algorithm that dynamically adjusts its parameters based on the observed system behavior, enabling efficient simulation and optimization of complex systems. The paper details the mechanism behind this adaptation, emphasizing the transformative impact of quantum properties on the algorithm's responsiveness and effectiveness. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual framework and preliminary simulations, highlighting the advantages of quantum topology in tackling complex problems.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Adaptive Matrix Decomposition
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a perplexing phenomenon of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum state decomposition, leveraging the unique properties of entangled states to achieve rapid and precise separations, and exploring its application to quantum computing. The core mechanism centers around designing a 'correlations matrix' computation method that dynamically adjusts entanglement strength, thereby enhancing computational accuracy and efficiency. We propose a new framework for efficiently manipulating entangled states, offering a potential breakthrough in tackling the limitations of current quantum computation techniques. This work contributes to the advancement of quantum algorithms and provides a foundational understanding of the potential of entanglement-based decomposition.

title: Title: Adaptive Constraint Optimization via Quantum Annealing (ACOQ)
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Constraint Optimization via Quantum Annealing (ACOQ), a novel optimization algorithm designed to address the limitations of traditional methods. Traditional optimization techniques often rely on static constraints, which can be suboptimal in dynamic environments. ACOQ leverages quantum annealing to dynamically adjust constraint constraints based on the system's response to the optimization process, offering a significant advantage in scenarios requiring real-time adaptation. This paper details the algorithm's architecture, the quantum annealing process, the adaptive constraint relaxation mechanism, and a comprehensive evaluation of its performance across a range of test cases. We demonstrate that ACOQ provides a substantial improvement in solution quality and computational efficiency compared to existing methods, particularly in problems exhibiting complex, dynamic constraints. The implementation showcases a successful application to a constrained optimization problem, illustrating the algorithm's potential for wider adoption in various fields.

title: Probabilistic Resonance Networks for Unsupervised Feature Discovery
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to unsupervised feature discovery within deep neural networks, utilizing "Probabilistic Resonance Networks" (PRNs). PRNs introduce a probabilistic layer designed to dynamically adjust connection strengths based on the principle of probabilistic resonance. This mechanism encourages neuronal activation patterns to resonate, effectively guiding the network towards the identification of relevant features without explicit supervision. The core innovation lies in shifting away from static connection weighting methods and embracing an active, adaptive network structure. We demonstrate that this approach can lead to more efficient and robust feature extraction, particularly in scenarios with evolving data distributions. The theoretical framework underpinning PRNs is presented, outlining the mathematical principles governing the stochastic resonance process and its impact on network dynamics. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications and future research directions for PRNs.

title: 基于动态规划的程序优化
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to program optimization utilizing dynamic programming. The core idea is to represent program execution paths as a dynamic programming table, allowing for the systematic identification and elimination of redundant operations. Unlike traditional heuristic optimization methods, this technique provides a deterministic and potentially more efficient solution by explicitly modeling the problem's structure and dependencies. The methodology involves transforming program code into a dynamic programming problem, formulating appropriate state transition functions, and employing dynamic programming algorithms to compute the optimal execution path. The presented framework offers a promising avenue for enhancing program performance, particularly in scenarios where the program's logic exhibits overlapping subproblems. This research demonstrates a significant departure from conventional optimization techniques, promising improved optimization results and reduced computational overhead.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum state self-adaptive topology analysis framework. The framework leverages machine learning to iteratively refine the topology, offering a new approach to quantum system design and stability enhancement. This work addresses the limitations of existing approaches by focusing on dynamic topology optimization, providing a robust and adaptable tool for quantum system analysis and control.
